questions.q: In software testing terminology, which term is defined as a measure of the difference between the actual and the ideal?
o: Failure
Error
Defect
Fault
questions.e: An error is defined as a measure of the difference between the actual and the ideal. This contrasts with a fault (a condition that causes a system to fail) and a failure (the inability to perform a required function).

questions.q: Which term refers to a condition that causes a system to fail in performing its required function?
o: Debugging
Fault
Error
Failure
questions.e: A fault is a condition that causes a system to fail in performing its required function. A failure, by contrast, is the actual inability of a system or component to perform a required function according to its specifications.

questions.q: Debugging is best described as which of the following activities?
o: The activity by which faults are identified and rectified
Determining whether a program produced the correct outcome
Demonstrating the presence of failures in a program
Devising inputs and predicted outputs to test a system
questions.e: Debugging is the activity by which faults are identified and rectified. Devising inputs with predicted outputs describes test cases, and determining correctness of an outcome describes a testing oracle.

questions.q: Under the rules used to identify a software bug, which situation qualifies as a bug?
o: The software runs faster than expected
The software is easy to understand and use
The software does exactly what the specification requires
The software does something that the specification says it should not do
questions.e: A software bug occurs when at least one bug rule is true, including when the software does something the specification says it should not do. Other rules cover failing to do what the spec requires, doing something the spec does not mention, and being difficult to understand, hard to use, or slow.

questions.q: If fixing a bug found during the specification stage costs $1, what is the approximate cost of fixing that same bug once it is found in released software, given that cost increases tenfold at each stage (specification, design, code, released)?
questions.e: The relative cost of bugs increases exponentially (10x) at each stage: $1 in specification, $10 in design, $100 in code, and $1000 in released software. Bugs found later cost more to fix.

questions.q: A testing oracle is best described as which of the following?
o: Inputs devised to test a system
The predicted output of a single test case
A mechanism that helps determine whether a program produced the correct outcome
A collection of test cases
questions.e: A testing oracle is a mechanism (a program, process, or body of data) that helps determine whether the program produced the correct outcome, often defined as a set of input/expected-outcome pairs. A collection of test cases is a test suite.

questions.q: A collection of test cases is referred to by which term?
o: Test data
Testing oracle
Test suite
Regression set
questions.e: A test suite is a collection of test cases. A testing oracle, by contrast, is a mechanism used to determine whether the program produced the correct outcome.

questions.q: Which of the following is identified as a source of testing oracles?
o: Boundary value analysis
Regression test suites developed for previous versions of the same software
Code and Fix models
Static source code analysis
questions.e: Sources of testing oracles include regression test suites (test suites developed for previous versions of the same software), purchased test suites for highly standardized software such as compilers, and an existing trusted program being re-hosted.

questions.q: What distinction is drawn between 'outcome' and 'output' in testing?
o: Outcome and output are always identical
An outcome is what we expect to happen and may differ from output; for example, a screen not changing is a tangible outcome with no output
Output includes intangible results while outcome is only visible screen changes
Output is what we expect while outcome is only the raw data produced
questions.e: An outcome is what we expect to happen as a result of a test, and in practice outcome and output may not be the same. For example, the screen not changing as a result of a test is a tangible outcome even though there is no output; in testing we are concerned with outcomes, not just outputs.

questions.q: According to the cited testing reality, roughly how many bugs do even good programs contain per 100 lines of code?
o: Less than 1 bug
10-20 bugs
1-3 bugs
5-10 bugs
questions.e: Studies show that even good programs have 1-3 bugs per 100 lines of code, and people who claim to write bug-free software probably have not programmed much.

questions.q: The NIST study cited in IEEE Software (Nov/Dec 2002) estimated the annual national cost of inadequate testing at approximately what figure?
o: $590 million
$59 billion
$590 billion
$5.9 billion
questions.e: The NIST study estimated the annual national cost of inadequate testing at as much as $59 billion. Some estimates also put testing at roughly 50% of development costs.

questions.q: Some estimates place testing at approximately what share of software development costs?
questions.e: Testing consumes substantial project resources, with some estimates putting it at about 50% of development costs.

questions.q: The principle 'Testing can show the presence of bugs, not their absence' is attributed to which set of initials?
o: IEEE
NIST
IBM
EWD
questions.e: The statement 'Testing can show the presence of bug, not their absence' is attributed to EWD (Edsger W. Dijkstra), reflecting that even exhaustive testing of all execution paths cannot guarantee correctness.

questions.q: Which three software development lifecycles are listed together?
o: Waterfall, V-Model, Agile
Code and Fix, Prototype, Incremental
Code and Fix, Waterfall, Spiral
Agile, Scrum, Kanban
questions.e: The three software development lifecycles named are Code and Fix, Waterfall, and Spiral.

questions.q: What is stated as the goal of a software tester?
o: To prove the program is perfect and free of all defects
To write the production code with structured programming
To eliminate the need for any specification
To find bugs as early in the development process as possible and make sure they get fixed
questions.e: The goal of a software tester is to find bugs as early in the software development process as possible and to make sure they get fixed, while avoiding the dangerous spiral of unattainable perfection.

questions.q: In the aviation bug examples, what caused an F-16 simulation to flip the virtual plane over whenever it crossed the equator?
o: The arithmetic sum being taken instead of the sum of absolute values
A missing exception condition in an if-then clause
An overflow of a 16-bit word
A missing minus sign to indicate south latitude
questions.e: In simulation, an F-16 program bug flipped the virtual plane over whenever it crossed the equator, caused by a missing minus sign to indicate south latitude. The separate F-18 crash was due to a missing exception condition (an if-then without the else clause).

questions.q: An F-18 crash was attributed to which type of software defect?
o: A year-2000 date interpretation error
A missing minus sign for south latitude
A missing exception condition: an if-then without the else clause thought impossible to reach
A 16-bit integer overflow
questions.e: An F-18 crashed because of a missing exception condition: an if-then without the else clause that was thought could not possibly arise. The missing minus sign for south latitude was the separate F-16 simulation bug.

questions.q: In the auto insurance 'year ambiguity' example, Mr. Blodgett's rate tripled when he turned 101 because his age was interpreted as 1. Why was this described as a double blunder?
o: Because the program's definition of a teenager is someone under 20
Because the program could not store ages above 100
Because his age was also interpreted as 200
Because the insurance rate should have been halved
questions.e: Mr. Blodgett was the program's first driver over 100, so his age of 101 was interpreted as 1. It was a double blunder because the program's definition of a teenager is someone under 20, meaning an age of 1 should not have triggered a high (teen-driver) rate.

questions.q: The number 32,768, cited as a source of computing grief, corresponds to which power of two and word size?
o: 2 to the 8th power, overflowing 16-bit words
2 to the 10th power, overflowing 8-bit words
2 to the 15th power, overflowing 16-bit words
2 to the 16th power, overflowing 32-bit words
questions.e: The number 32,768 equals 2 to the 15th power and caused all sorts of grief from the overflowing of 16-bit words.

questions.q: In the nuclear reactor simulation fault that led five US plants to be shut down in 1979, what was the underlying arithmetic mistake?
o: The absolute values were summed instead of the arithmetic sum
The arithmetic sum of a set of numbers was taken instead of the sum of their absolute values
The numbers were multiplied instead of added
A minus sign was omitted from the calculation
questions.e: The fault occurred because the arithmetic sum of a set of numbers was taken instead of the sum of the absolute values, and it was discovered only after the power plants were built.

questions.q: In the Therac-25 Washington 1987 incident, what radiation dose did the patient receive compared to what was prescribed?
o: 8,000-10,000 rads instead of the prescribed 86 rads
4,000 rads instead of the prescribed 800 rads
86 rads instead of the prescribed 8,000 rads
16,500-25,000 rads instead of the prescribed 86 rads
questions.e: In the Washington 1987 Therac-25 case, a patient received 8,000-10,000 rads instead of the prescribed 86 rads and died of complications of the radiation overdose.

questions.q: A UK bank software flaw that duplicated every transfer payment request for half an hour resulted in what loss?
o: The bank permanently lost 2 billion British pounds
The bank lost 2 billion British pounds, later recovered, but lost half a million pounds in potential interest
The bank lost half a billion pounds that was never recovered
An ATM dispensed 10 times the required amount
questions.e: A software flaw caused a UK bank to duplicate every transfer payment request for half an hour, losing 2 billion British pounds. The bank eventually recovered the funds but lost half a million pounds in potential interest. The 10-times-dispensing incident was a separate Norwegian ATM case.

questions.q: In program testing, a 'successful test' is characterized as which of the following?
o: A test which discovers one or more faults
A test that runs faster than expected
A test that confirms the program has no bugs
A test that produces no output
questions.e: A successful test is a test which discovers one or more faults. Correspondingly, a successful defect test is one that causes a program to behave in an anomalous way; tests show the presence, not the absence, of defects.

questions.q: Which statement reflects the stated testing priorities?
o: Testing typical situations is more important than boundary value cases
Tests should exercise components rather than capabilities
Testing new capabilities is more important than testing old capabilities
Testing boundary value cases is more important than typical situations
questions.e: The testing priorities state that testing typical situations is more important than boundary value cases, testing old capabilities is more important than new ones, and tests should exercise a system's capabilities rather than its components.

questions.q: Which comparison between testing and debugging is correct?
o: Neither testing nor debugging can be performed by an outsider
Debugging can be automated to a large extent while testing cannot
Both testing and debugging require detailed design knowledge by an insider
Testing can be automated to a large extent while automatic debugging is still a dream
questions.e: Testing can be automated to a large extent, whereas automatic debugging is still a dream. Much of testing can be done without design knowledge (by an outsider), while debugging is impossible without detailed design knowledge (by an insider).

questions.q: How are 'test data' and 'test cases' distinguished from each other?
o: Test data are inputs devised to test the system, while test cases are inputs together with the predicted outputs if the system operates to specification
Test cases are collections of test data with no predicted outcomes
Test data are inputs plus predicted outputs, while test cases are only inputs
Test data and test cases are identical concepts
questions.e: Test data are inputs which have been devised to test the system, while test cases are inputs to test the system together with the predicted outputs from those inputs assuming the system operates according to its specification.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a source of problems in software development?
o: Using good programming languages
Overly simple software architecture
Requirements Definition producing erroneous, incomplete, or inconsistent requirements
Excessive testing of software
questions.e: The listed sources of problems include Requirements Definition (erroneous, incomplete, inconsistent requirements), Design flaws, Implementation mistakes, poor Support Systems, Inadequate Testing, and Evolution (sloppy maintenance).

questions.q: Besides testing, which of the following is named as another method for improving software reliability?
o: Removing all specifications
Avoiding compilers and type checking
Increasing the number of released bugs
Inspection methods such as walkthroughs, formal inspections, and code reading
questions.e: Other methods for improving software reliability include inspection methods (walkthroughs, formal inspections, code reading), design style, static analysis (compilers handling type checking), and good programming languages and tools such as Lint.

questions.q: Which testing approach uses the source code as the point of reference for test selection and adequacy?
o: Beta testing
White-box (structural) testing
Black-box (functional) testing
Acceptance testing
questions.e: White-box testing, also called glass-box or structural testing (a.k.a. program-based testing), uses the source code as the reference for selecting test cases and judging adequacy, whereas black-box testing uses the specification instead.

questions.q: Black-box testing is also known by which alternative name?
o: Structural testing
Glass-box testing
Specification-based testing
Program-based testing
questions.e: Black-box (functional) testing is also called specification-based testing because it uses the specification as the reference for test selection; the structural, glass-box, and program-based names all refer to white-box testing.

questions.q: Which characteristic is associated with black-box testing rather than white-box testing?
o: Test planning can begin early and criteria are not precise
Requires the programmer's knowledge of the source code
Aims at exercising the different control and data structures in the program
Criteria are quite precise because they are based on program structures
questions.e: Black-box testing treats the program as a black box where implementation details do not matter, its criteria are not precise, and test planning can begin early. Precise criteria based on program structures and needing source-code knowledge are white-box traits.

questions.q: White-box testing makes which assumption about the source code?
o: That the source code fully implements the specification
That criteria cannot be precise
That an end-user perspective is required
That implementation details do not matter
questions.e: White-box testing assumes that the source code fully implements the specification; it looks at implementation details and requires the programmer's knowledge of the code, which contrasts with black-box testing's end-user perspective.

questions.q: What is described as the real difference between white-box and black-box testing?
o: Whether the program's correctness is checked at all
How test cases are generated and how adequacy is determined
Whether the testing can be made exhaustive
Whether specifications are used to check correctness
questions.e: The real difference lies in how test cases are generated and how adequacy is determined. In both approaches correctness is usually checked via specifications, neither can be exhaustive, and both should be used.

questions.q: Is complete testing possible for non-trivial software?
o: Yes, but only with white-box techniques
No, but it is theoretically possible
Yes, if enough test drivers are used
No, it is both practically and theoretically impossible
questions.e: Complete testing is both practically and theoretically impossible for non-trivial software; complete functional testing would require all possible input streams and complete structural testing faces non-terminating or too-numerous paths.

questions.q: For a program with an input stream of only 10 characters, at 1 microsecond per test, how long would exhaustive functional testing take?
o: About one year
More time than twice the current estimated age of the universe
Less than one day
Exactly the estimated age of the universe
questions.e: Even with just a 10-character input stream, exhaustive functional testing at 1 microsecond per test would require more time than twice the current estimated age of the universe, illustrating why complete functional testing is infeasible.

questions.q: In complete structural testing, tests should ensure that every path is executed at least once. What problem is raised against achieving this?
o: The source code is unavailable to the tester
Criteria are not precise enough to design tests
The specification does not describe the paths
Loops may never terminate, and even if they do the number of paths may be too large
questions.e: Complete structural testing aims to execute every path at least once, but loops may never terminate and, even when they do, the number of paths may be too large, making the goal impractical.

questions.q: What is stated as a drawback of using correctness proofs in practice?
o: Program statements cannot be used in inductive proofs
Requirements cannot be specified formally
Such proofs are time consuming and expensive
They can only be applied to black-box testing
questions.e: Correctness proofs specify requirements in a formal language and use each program statement in a step of an inductive proof, but in practice such proofs are time consuming and expensive.

questions.q: Which is identified as an advantage of bottom-up integration testing?
o: No test stubs are needed
No test drivers are needed
Interface errors are discovered early
The whole system is available at once
questions.e: In bottom-up integration, no test stubs are needed and errors in critical modules are found early. Its disadvantages are that test drivers are needed and interface errors are discovered late.

questions.q: Who performs unit testing and what form of testing is it considered?
o: Each developer; white-box form of testing
A separate group within the organization; black-box testing
The end-users; acceptance testing
A small team; incremental integration testing
questions.e: Unit testing is performed by each developer to ensure each module (class, subprogram) or collection of modules has been implemented correctly, and it is a white-box form of testing.

questions.q: In a unit test environment, which supporting components substitute for the module's called and calling routines?
o: Reviews and inspections
Use-cases and scenarios
A driver and stubs
Clusters and builds
questions.e: The unit test environment uses a driver to invoke the module under test and stubs to stand in for called modules, while test cases exercise local data structures, boundary conditions, error handling paths, and interfaces.

questions.q: What is the scope of integration testing?
o: Re-test modified software after changes
Ensure that the interfaces between components have been implemented correctly
Ensure that each individual module has been implemented correctly
Pretend to be the end-users of the product
questions.e: Integration testing, performed by a small team, ensures that the interfaces between components (which developers could not test on their own) have been implemented correctly, using approaches such as big-bang or incremental construction.

questions.q: In top-down integration, how are stubs handled as integration proceeds?
o: Stubs are replaced one at a time, depth first, with some subset of tests re-run
Worker modules are grouped into builds and integrated
Drivers are replaced one at a time, depth first
All stubs are replaced simultaneously in a big-bang
questions.e: In top-down integration the top module is tested with stubs, then stubs are replaced one at a time in a depth-first manner, and as new modules are integrated some subset of tests is re-run.

questions.q: Which is stated as a disadvantage of the big-bang integration approach?
o: The whole system is never available
It is harder to locate errors
Focus is placed too narrowly on each single module
Special stub and driver code must be developed
questions.e: Big-bang integration makes it harder to locate errors, is hard to guarantee all components are ready at once, and does not focus on a specific component; its advantage is that the whole system is available. Needing special stub/driver code is instead a disadvantage of incremental integration.

questions.q: How is system testing characterized in terms of who performs it and its form?
o: Performed by end-users; acceptance testing
Performed by each developer; white-box form of testing
Performed by a small team; incremental testing
Performed by a separate group in the organization; black-box form of testing
questions.e: System testing is performed by a separate group within the organization that pretends to be the end-users; it is a black-box form of testing with test case specification driven by use-cases.

questions.q: During system testing, adequacy is based on what?
o: Requirements coverage, while thinking beyond stated requirements
Path coverage of the source code
The number of stubs and drivers developed
Coverage of module interfaces
questions.e: In system testing, adequacy is based on requirements coverage, but testers must also think beyond the stated requirements; the effort is captured in a System Test Plan with designed, documented, and reviewed test cases.

questions.q: Which type of testing executes a system in a manner that demands resources in abnormal quantity, frequency, or volume?
o: Stress testing
Recovery testing
Usability testing
Performance testing
questions.e: Stress testing executes a system in a manner that demands resources in abnormal quantity, frequency, or volume. Recovery testing forces failures to verify recovery, and performance testing checks run-time performance.

questions.q: Which type of testing forces the software to fail in various ways and verifies that recovery is properly performed?
o: Stress testing
Recovery testing
Reliability testing
Security testing
questions.e: Recovery testing forces the software to fail in a variety of ways and verifies that recovery is properly performed, whereas security testing verifies protection mechanisms against improper penetration.

questions.q: Regression testing is the activity of what, and which options does it offer?
o: Testing component interfaces; big-bang, incremental, or sandwich
Testing run-time performance; top-down or bottom-up
Re-testing modified software; retest-none, retest-all, or selective retesting
Verifying protection mechanisms; alpha, beta, or acceptance
questions.e: Regression testing is the activity of re-testing modified software, since changes commonly introduce problems; its options are retest-none, retest-all, and selective retesting, and it can be fairly expensive for some systems.

questions.q: According to the definition of quality attributed to IEEE, quality is what?
o: Fault prevention through process design and auditing
The totality of features and characteristics that satisfy stated or implied needs
Conformance to explicitly stated requirements and implicit professional characteristics
The degree to which a system, component, or process meets specified requirements and user needs
questions.e: The IEEE definition describes quality as the degree to which a system, component, or process meets specified requirements and the degree to which it meets customer or user needs or expectations; the conformance-oriented definition is credited to Pressman.

questions.q: According to a 2002 US Department of Commerce figure, what was the estimated annual cost of software bugs to the U.S. economy?
o: $59.5 billion, about 0.6 percent of GDP
$59.5 billion, about 6 percent of GDP
$22.2 billion, about 0.6 percent of GDP
$22.2 billion, about 0.2 percent of GDP
questions.e: Software bugs were estimated to cost the U.S. economy about $59.5 billion annually, or roughly 0.6 percent of GDP; of this, an estimated $22.2 billion could be eliminated by improved testing infrastructure.

questions.q: In the given definitions, which term is specifically identified as the terminology of the tester?
o: Defect
Failure
Bug
Fault
questions.e: A bug is defined as a fault in a program causing unintended or unanticipated behavior, and it is noted as the terminology of the tester; a fault is an incorrect step, process, or data definition.

questions.q: How is a software failure defined?
o: The inability of a system or component to perform its required functions within specified performance requirements
Troubles with the software's external behavior or internal features
An incorrect step, process, or data definition in a program
A discrepancy between a computed value and the true or specified value
questions.e: A software failure is the inability of a system or component to perform its required functions within specified performance requirements; the discrepancy-in-value definition describes a software error instead.

questions.q: Under the product operations category of quality attributes, which attribute is listed?
o: Portability
Reusability
Maintainability
Reliability
questions.e: Product operations related attributes include reliability, robustness, efficiency, usability, safety, security, and fault-tolerance. Portability and reusability are product-transition related, while maintainability is product-revision related.

questions.q: Maintainability is classified under which category of quality attributes?
o: Product transition related
Product revision related
Functional requirements
Product operations related
questions.e: Maintainability is a product-revision related attribute. Product-transition related attributes are portability, interoperability, and reusability, while product-operations related attributes include reliability and security.

questions.q: How is quality assurance distinguished from quality control?
o: QA examines artefacts against criteria, while QC creates processes and tools
QA detects faults through testing, while QC prevents them through process design
QA and QC both refer only to dynamic testing
QA is fault prevention through process design and auditing, while QC is fault/failure detection through testing of artefacts
questions.e: Quality assurance is fault prevention through process design and auditing (creating processes and tools to prevent defect injection), whereas quality control is fault/failure detection through static and/or dynamic testing of artefacts against pre-determined criteria.

questions.q: Which quality control method is associated with proofs of correctness?
o: Reviews
Mathematical
Simulations
Field trials
questions.e: Among quality control methods, the mathematical method corresponds to proofs of correctness; reviews cover personal, peer, and pair reviews, simulations cover prototypes and models, and field trials cover prototypes and beta testing.

questions.q: Software quality engineering is described as what kind of process?
o: A one-time planning activity performed before development
An iterative process combining quality planning, assurance, and control activities
A purely mathematical proof activity
A phase performed only after system testing
questions.e: The quality engineering process is an iterative process which combines quality planning, quality assurance, and quality control activities, with the goal of defect prevention, reduction, and containment.

questions.q: Which two quality standards are named as topics in this material?
o: IEEE 829 and Six Sigma
ISO 27001 and TQM
CMMI and ITIL
ISO 9000 standards and the Capability Maturity Model (CMM)
questions.e: The quality standards named are the ISO 9000 standards and the Capability Maturity Model (CMM), both left for a later lecture.

questions.q: Quality attributes, against which stated or implied needs are tested, are said to be part of which document?
o: The quality plan
The incident report library
The Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
The System Test Plan
questions.e: Quality attributes are the quality features and characteristics that form part of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document, and quality control, measurement, and inspection techniques are employed against them.

questions.q: When does test planning usually start, and what does it define?
o: During integration; it defines only tool availability
During system testing; it defines only the test completion criteria
After acceptance testing; it defines the quality attributes
During the requirements phase; it defines the functions, roles, and methods for all test phases
questions.e: Test planning usually starts during the requirements phase and defines the functions, roles, and methods for all test phases; its major elements include objectives, schedules and responsibilities, tool/facility/library availability, and test completion criteria.

questions.q: A Control Flow Graph (CFG) is formally defined as a directed graph G = (N, E). What do the elements of the set N represent?
o: Only the entry and exit points of the program
Test inputs and their expected outputs
Def-use pairs of variables
Statement nodes or predicate nodes
questions.e: A CFG is a directed graph G = (N, E) where each node in N is either a statement node (a simple statement or basic block) or a predicate node (a conditional statement). Edges in E represent the flow of control.

questions.q: In a Control Flow Graph, what does an edge in the set E represent?
o: An infeasible path
A basic block of assignments
A conditional statement
The flow of control between statements
questions.e: Each edge in the set E represents the flow of control between statements, while nodes represent statements or predicates.

questions.q: When drawing a Control Flow Graph with the optional shape convention, which shapes are used for statement nodes and predicate nodes respectively?
o: Diamonds for statements and ovals for predicates
Squares for both, distinguished by color
Rectangles for statements and circles for predicates
Circles for statements and rectangles for predicates
questions.e: The optional convention uses circles to represent statement nodes and rectangles to represent predicate nodes. A predicate node represents a conditional statement.

questions.q: How is a program path defined?
o: A sequence of statements from entry to exit
Any conditional statement that alters the default flow
A pair of locations where a variable is defined and used
The subset of variables defined at a node
questions.e: A program path is a sequence of statements from entry to exit. There can be a large number of paths in a program, and there is an (input, expected output) pair for each path.

questions.q: Two kinds of basic program statements are distinguished when constructing a CFG. Which pairing is correct?
o: Node statements and edge statements
Executable statements and infeasible statements
Def statements and kill statements
Assignment statements (e.g., x = 2*y) and conditional statements (e.g., if(), for(), while())
questions.e: The two kinds of basic program statements are assignment statements such as x = 2*y, and conditional statements such as if(), for(), and while(). Conditional statements alter the default flow of control.

questions.q: During test generation from a CFG, two kinds of paths are distinguished. Which statement correctly describes an infeasible path?
o: A path for which there is no input to execute the path
A path that provides complete statement coverage
A path for which there exists input so that the path is executed
A simple path that is def-clear from a def to a use
questions.e: An infeasible path is one for which there is no input to execute the path, in contrast to an executable path, for which there exists input so that the path is executed.

questions.q: In the CFG treatment of a switch-case construct, what important observation is made about the switch expression e?
o: e is not a predicate
e must be an assignment statement
e is a predicate node with two outgoing edges
e is always an infeasible path
questions.e: Although the switch-case diagram intuitively resembles a decision, the switch expression e is not a predicate, because it can branch to multiple cases (v1, v2, default) rather than a simple true/false outcome.

questions.q: Which definition correctly distinguishes a software fault from a software failure?
o: A fault and a failure both refer to an execution that results in a failure
A fault is external incorrect behavior, while a failure is a static defect
A fault is an incorrect internal state, while a failure is a static defect
A fault is a static defect in the software, while a failure is external, incorrect behavior with respect to the requirements
questions.e: A software fault is a static defect in the software, whereas a software failure is external, incorrect behavior with respect to the requirements or other description of expected behavior.

questions.q: How is a software error defined?
o: A static defect in the software
An execution that results in a failure
External, incorrect behavior with respect to requirements
An incorrect internal state that is the manifestation of some fault
questions.e: A software error is an incorrect internal state that is the manifestation of some fault. This is distinct from a fault (a static defect) and a failure (external incorrect behavior).

questions.q: What is a test requirement?
o: A specific element of a software artifact that a test case must satisfy or cover
A path for which no input exists to execute it
A two-character sequence denoting a data-flow anomaly
The number of test cases needed to achieve full coverage
questions.e: A test requirement is a specific element of a software artifact that a test case must satisfy or cover. Program paths are selectively executed to meet test requirements.

questions.q: Which of the following is stated as an advantage of selecting paths based on defined criteria?
o: It eliminates all infeasible paths automatically
It ensures that all program constructs are executed at least once
It removes the need for a control flow graph
It guarantees the smallest possible number of test cases
questions.e: Advantages of selecting paths based on defined criteria include ensuring all program constructs are executed at least once, avoiding repeated selection of the same path, and easily identifying which features have been tested.

questions.q: Statement Coverage is achieved under which condition?
o: When all nodes in the graph have been executed
When every boolean variable evaluates to both TRUE and FALSE
When all edges in the graph have been executed
When all statements in a method have been executed at least once
questions.e: Statement Coverage is achieved when all statements in a method have been executed at least once. Node Coverage requires all nodes executed and Edge Coverage requires all edges executed.

questions.q: For the code IF ((x || y) && z) a = b + c;, what does Condition Coverage require?
o: That every statement is executed at least once
That every du-path from a def to a use is toured
That the IF statement as a whole evaluates to TRUE and FALSE at least once
That each boolean expression X, Y and Z is evaluated to TRUE and FALSE at least one time
questions.e: Condition Coverage requires that each individual boolean expression (X, Y and Z) in the statement be evaluated to both TRUE and FALSE at least one time. Deciding the whole IF outcome is instead Decision Coverage.

questions.q: For the code IF ((x || y) && z) a = b + c;, what does Decision Coverage require?
o: That each variable independently affects the decision outcome
That each of x, y and z individually takes both TRUE and FALSE
That all du-paths for the variables are covered
That the IF statement evaluates to TRUE and FALSE at least once
questions.e: Decision Coverage requires ensuring that the IF statement (the decision) evaluates to both TRUE and FALSE at least once, which for this example is satisfied by T1: X=T,Y=T,Z=T and T2: X=F,Y=F,Z=F.

questions.q: What additional requirement does Modified/Multiple Condition Decision Coverage (MCDC) add beyond Condition Coverage?
o: Every node and every edge must be covered simultaneously
Each Boolean variable must be evaluated to TRUE and FALSE at least once and also affect the decision outcome
Each statement must be executed at least twice
All infeasible paths must be identified and removed
questions.e: MCDC requires that each Boolean variable be evaluated to both TRUE and FALSE at least once and also independently affect the decision outcome, going beyond plain Condition Coverage.

questions.q: How is criteria subsumption defined?
o: A test criterion C1 subsumes C2 if both cover the same nodes
A test criterion C1 subsumes C2 only when C2 is infeasible
A test criterion C1 subsumes C2 if and only if every set of test cases that satisfies C1 also satisfies C2
A test criterion C1 subsumes C2 if C1 uses fewer test cases than C2
questions.e: Criteria subsumption states that a test criterion C1 subsumes C2 if and only if every set of test cases that satisfies criterion C1 also satisfies C2. For example, Edge Coverage subsumes Node coverage.

questions.q: Which subsumption relationship between coverage criteria is stated to hold?
o: Edge Coverage subsumes Node Coverage
Condition Coverage subsumes All-du-Paths
Statement Coverage subsumes MCDC
Node Coverage subsumes Edge Coverage
questions.e: Edge Coverage subsumes Node coverage: every set of test cases that satisfies Edge Coverage also satisfies Node Coverage. It is also noted that coverage does not depend on the number of test cases.

questions.q: What is data-flow testing?
o: A family of test strategies based on selecting paths through the program's control flow to explore sequences of events related to the status of data objects
A method that ignores the control flow graph entirely
A criterion that requires executing every statement exactly once
A technique that counts the number of edges to compute cyclomatic complexity
questions.e: Data-flow testing is the name given to a family of test strategies based on selecting paths through the program's control flow in order to explore sequences of events related to the status of data objects, such as ensuring every data object is initialized before use.

questions.q: In data-flow annotation of a CFG, what do the letters d, k and u denote?
o: defined, killed, and used
default, kernel, and update
declared, kept, and unused
def-pair, kill-pair, and use-pair
questions.e: CFG annotations use (d) for Defined/Created/Initialized, (k) for Killed/Undefined/Released, and (u) for Used, where a use can be (c) used in a calculation or (p) used in a predicate.

questions.q: A variable is considered used for a computation (c-use) when it appears where in an assignment statement?
o: Only inside a predicate
Only on the left-hand side (LHS)
Only when the variable is declared
On the right-hand side (RHS), and sometimes the LHS in the case of array indices
questions.e: A variable is used for a computation (c) when it appears on the RHS of an assignment statement, and sometimes even on the LHS in the case of array indices. A p-use is when the variable appears directly in a predicate.

questions.q: A data-flow anomaly is denoted by a two-character sequence of actions. What does the sequence dd mean?
o: An object is defined and then killed
An object is killed and then used
An object is used and then defined
An object is defined twice without an intervening usage
questions.e: The dd anomaly means that an object is defined twice without an intervening usage. It is described as probably harmless but suspicious.

questions.q: Among the two-letter data-flow situations, which one is classified as 'Definitely a bug'?
o: dd
ku
du
ud
questions.e: The ku situation (an object is killed and then used) is classified as definitely a bug. By contrast dd is suspicious, du is normal, and ud is a normal reassignment.

questions.q: Which two-letter data-flow situation is described as 'Probably a bug'?
o: dk
uu
du
kd
questions.e: The dk situation (defined then killed) is described as probably a bug. In contrast du, kd, and uu are all described as normal situations.

questions.q: How is a du-pair defined?
o: A pair of test cases that together achieve branch coverage
A pair consisting of a fault and its resulting failure
A pair of adjacent nodes connected by a control-flow edge
A pair of locations (li, lj) such that variable v is defined at li and used at lj
questions.e: A du-pair is a pair of locations (li, lj) such that variable v is defined at li and used at lj. Values are carried from their defs to uses.

questions.q: A path from li to lj is called a def-clear path with respect to variable v under what condition?
o: If v is killed at both li and lj
If the path is infeasible
If v is not given another value on any of the nodes or edges in the path
If v is used at least once on every node in the path
questions.e: A path from li to lj is a def-clear path with respect to variable v if v is not given another value on any of the nodes or edges in the path, meaning the def of v at li reaches the use at lj.

questions.q: Which properties characterize a du-path with respect to a variable v?
o: It must be a non-simple path that revisits nodes
It ignores the variable and covers all nodes
It is a simple path, def-clear from a def of v to a use of v, and may have intervening uses
It must contain a kill of v between the def and the use
questions.e: A du-path with respect to variable v is a simple path that is def-clear from a def of v to a use of v; du-paths are parameterized by v, need to be simple paths, and there may be intervening uses on the path.

questions.q: Under All-Defs Coverage, what must the test requirements guarantee?
o: Every def reaches at least one use
Every def reaches every possible use
Every def reaches every use through every possible du-path
Every node and edge is covered
questions.e: All-Defs Coverage requires that for each def-path set S = du(n, v), the test requirements contain at least one path in S, so that every def reaches at least one use.

questions.q: How does All-Uses Coverage differ from All-du-Paths Coverage?
o: All-Uses requires touring every du-path, while All-du-Paths requires only one use per def
All-Uses only covers nodes, while All-du-Paths only covers edges
They are identical criteria
All-Uses requires every def to reach every use, while All-du-Paths requires every def to reach every use through every possible du-path
questions.e: All-Uses Coverage requires that every def reach every use (at least one path per def-use pair), whereas All-du-Paths Coverage requires that every def reach every use through every possible du-path (every path in each def-pair set).

questions.q: In the data-flow subsumption hierarchy, which criterion sits at the very top, subsuming all the others?
o: ALL-PATHS
ALL-DEFS
ALL-NODES
ALL-EDGES
questions.e: In the subsumption hierarchy, ALL-PATHS is at the top, above ALL-DU-PATHS and ALL-USES, while ALL-NODES sits at the bottom as the weakest criterion.

questions.q: When a c-use of variable v is present, how is that use referenced in data-flow notation?
o: du(ni, v)
dcu(li, lj, v)
def(n)
dpu(li, (lj, lt), v)
questions.e: If v is used in a c-use, the use is referred to as dcu(li, lj, v). A p-use is instead represented as a set of two def-use pairs dpu(li, (lj, lt), v) and dpu(li, (lj, lf), v) for the true and false flow directions.

questions.q: A p-use of variable v is represented as a set of two def-use pairs, dpu(li, (lj, lt), v) and dpu(li, (lj, lf), v). What accounts for the two pairs?
o: The variable is used twice at the same node
The variable is defined at two different locations
One pair is for c-use and the other for k-use
v is used at lj having two flow directions, the true edge (lj, lt) and the false edge (lj, lf)
questions.e: Because a predicate has two flow directions, v defined at li and used at lj yields two pairs: one for the true edge (lj, lt) and one for the false edge (lj, lf), hence dpu(li, (lj, lt), v) and dpu(li, (lj, lf), v).

questions.q: In the 'big picture' of testing techniques, which techniques are associated with Unit Testing?
o: SRS and requirements review
Specification-based and Model-based techniques
CFG and DFG
MM Path and State-Machine
questions.e: Unit Testing techniques are listed as CFG and DFG (data flow graph). Integration Testing uses MM Path and State-Machine, while System Testing uses Specification-based and Model-based techniques.

questions.q: Which artifact is identified as the primary input for each of Unit, Integration, and System testing respectively?
o: Code + Design; SRS; Code
SRS; Code; Design
Code; Code + Design; SRS
Design; SRS; Code
questions.e: The artifacts are Code for Unit Testing, Code + Design for Integration Testing, and the SRS for System Testing.

questions.q: An object is described as killed when it is which of the following?
o: Assigned a new value or dynamically allocated
Appearing on the RHS of an assignment
Appearing directly in a predicate
Released (e.g., free) or otherwise made unavailable, such as going out of scope
questions.e: An object is killed when it is released (e.g., free) or otherwise made unavailable (e.g., out of scope), when a loop control variable's loop exits, or when a file is closed. Being assigned a new value or allocated corresponds to a def.

questions.q: For single-letter data-flow situations, what does a leading dash (as in -k) indicate?
o: Nothing of interest (d, k, u) occurs prior to the noted action along the entry-exit path of interest
The variable is guaranteed to be global
The variable is definitely killed twice
Nothing of interest happens after the point of action until exit
questions.e: A leading dash means nothing of interest (d, k, u) occurs prior to the action noted along the entry-exit path of interest; a trailing dash means nothing of interest happens after the point of action until exit.

questions.q: Two structural unit-testing techniques are contrasted for selecting a suitable unit testing approach. Which pair correctly names them?
o: Mutation-based technique and slice-based technique
Control-flow based technique and dataflow based technique
Boundary-value technique and equivalence-partitioning technique
State-based technique and decision-table technique
questions.e: When planning for unit testing, the two techniques presented for choosing a suitable approach are the control-flow based technique and the dataflow based technique. The other pairs name unrelated black-box or advanced techniques not offered as the two known options.

questions.q: In the three-step unit testing process, what is the first step performed before designing test cases?
o: Generate coverage report
Acquire test I/O pairs
Plan for unit testing
Execute unit test
questions.e: The process is ordered: (1) Plan for unit testing, (2) Design test cases and acquire test I/O pairs, (3) Execute unit test. Planning comes first; executing and generating coverage happen later, and acquiring I/O pairs is part of the second step.

questions.q: During the 'Plan for unit testing' step, which activity is carried out in addition to selecting a technique and acquiring the code?
o: Deciding which coverage criteria would be useful
Combining methods across classes
Executing the test stubs
Writing the coverage report
questions.e: The planning step involves selecting a suitable unit testing technique, acquiring the code for testing, and deciding which coverage criteria would be useful. Writing the report and executing stubs belong to later steps, and method combination relates to integration-level testing.

questions.q: Which ordered sequence of steps is used to derive test cases from a control-flow graph?
o: Develop CFG, find conditions, find inputs, find paths, derive test cases
Develop CFG, find paths through CFG, find path conditions, find appropriate inputs, derive test cases
Find inputs, develop CFG, find paths, find conditions, derive test cases
Derive test cases, find paths, develop CFG, find conditions, find inputs
questions.e: The correct order is: develop the CFG, find paths through the CFG, find path conditions, find appropriate inputs, and finally derive test cases as ({inputs}, expected output). The other orderings scramble these steps.

questions.q: A test case is expressed as which of the following pairings?
o: ({inputs...}, expected output)
(node count, edge count)
(statement, branch)
(path predicate, coverage percentage)
questions.e: A derived test case is written as ({inputs...}, expected output), pairing a set of input values with the expected result. The other options describe metrics or graph properties, not the test case form.

questions.q: For the binary-search example, the path 1, 2, 3, 8, 9 is associated with which condition and test case?
o: found == true; test case 3, {3,2}, 2
bottom > top; test case 0, {}, -1
bottom < top && found == false, elemArray[mid] == key; test case 1, {1,2,3,4}, 0
elemArray[mid] < key; test case 2, {1,2,3}, 1
questions.e: The path table gives path 1, 2, 3, 8, 9 the condition 'Bottom < top && found == false' with 'elemArray[mid] == key', and the test case 1, {1,2,3,4}, 0. The other conditions and test cases correspond to different paths.

questions.q: Which set of paths through the binary-search CFG is required so that test cases execute all of them?
questions.e: The four listed paths to be exercised are 1,2,3,8,9; 1,2,3,4,6,7,2; 1,2,3,4,5,7,2; and 1,2,3,4,6,7,2,8,9. Test cases should be derived so that all of these paths are executed.

questions.q: In the Visual Studio unit test example, which assertion is used to check that search returns the expected value?
o: Assert.AreEqual(1, bs.search(key, array))
Assert.IsTrue(bs.search(key, array))
Assert.IsNull(bs.search(key, array))
Assert.Fail(bs.search(key, array))
questions.e: The test method calls Assert.AreEqual(1, bs.search(key, array)) to compare the expected value 1 against the method's return. The other assertion forms check truth, force failure, or check for null instead of equality.

questions.q: When organizing unit tests in Visual Studio, how are code and test cases arranged in the solution?
o: Tests replace the code under test
Test cases are embedded inside the code file
Both are placed in a single shared class
A separate test project is added, keeping code and test cases separate
questions.e: The recommended arrangement is to add a separate test project in the solution, keeping code and test cases separate. Embedding tests in the code or merging them into one class is not the approach described.

questions.q: A program slice is best defined as which of the following?
o: A subset of a program that filters out code not relevant to the computation of interest
A performance profile of the program
A superset of the program including test stubs
A complete copy of the program
questions.e: A program slice is a subset of a program; slicing lets programmers view subsets by filtering out code that is not relevant to the computation of interest, such as isolating only the code that computes an average. It is neither a full copy nor a profile.

questions.q: For a program P and a set of variables V at location n, what does the slice S(V,n) produce?
o: The full call graph of P
The statements executed after location n
The portions of the program that contribute to the value of V just before the statement at location n is executed
All statements that never affect V
questions.e: S(V,n) produces the portions of the program that contribute to the value of V just before the statement at location n is executed; S(V,n) is called the slicing criteria. It concerns contributions before n, not statements after it.

questions.q: The notation S(V,n) is given a specific name. What is it called?
o: The dominator set
The coverage criterion
The path predicate
The slicing criteria
questions.e: S(V,n), where V is the set of variables at location n, is called the slicing criteria. Path predicate and coverage criterion are separate testing concepts, and dominator set is not mentioned.

questions.q: Which is one of the stated conditions that a valid program slice S(V,n) must satisfy?
o: It must change the value of V at location n
It must add new statements to P
It must be derived from P by deleting statements from P and be syntactically correct
It must be written in a different language than P
questions.e: A valid slice must be derived from P by deleting statements, must be syntactically correct, and for all executions the value of V just before location n must match that of P. Adding statements or changing V's value would violate these conditions.

questions.q: How is a static slice characterized?
o: It contains only statements affected by the slicing criterion
It is derived from source code, makes no assumption about input values, and contains all statements that may affect a variable
It is computed with respect to program history and is relatively small
It uses information about a particular execution
questions.e: A static slice is derived from source code, makes no assumption about input values, and contains all statements that may affect a variable. Using execution information and being small with respect to program history describe a dynamic slice instead.

questions.q: Which description matches a dynamic slice?
o: Contains all statements that may affect a variable regardless of execution
Is always larger than the corresponding static slice
Makes no assumption about input values
Uses information about a particular execution, is monitored, and is relatively small compared to a static slice
questions.e: A dynamic slice uses information about a particular execution; execution is monitored and the slice is computed with respect to program history, making it relatively small compared to a static slice while containing statements actually affecting a variable. Making no input assumptions describes a static slice.

questions.q: Which slicing technique is described as a bridge between the static and dynamic extremes?
o: Interface slicing
Forward slicing
Backward slicing
Conditional or quasi-static slicing
questions.e: The conditional or quasi-static slicing technique acts as a bridge between the two extremes, static and dynamic slicing. Backward, forward, and interface slicing are other slice categories, not the bridging technique.

questions.q: What distinguishes a backward slice from a forward slice?
o: A backward slice contains statements that may affect the slicing criterion, while a forward slice contains statements affected by the slicing criterion
A backward slice is always dynamic and a forward slice is always static
Both contain identical statements
A backward slice contains statements affected by the criterion, while a forward slice contains statements that affect it
questions.e: A backward slice contains statements of program P that may have some effect on the slicing criterion, whereas a forward slice contains statements affected by the slicing criterion S(V,n). Reversing these two definitions is a common error.

questions.q: Regarding a slice S(X,n) where variable X depends on variable Y, which observation holds?
o: All d-uses and p-uses of Y before n are included, while c-uses of Y have no effect on X unless X is a d-use in that statement
Only c-uses of Y before n are included
No uses of Y are ever included
p-uses of Y are excluded but c-uses are always included
questions.e: For S(X,n) with X depending on Y, all d-uses and p-uses of Y before n are included, and the c-uses of Y will have no effect on X unless X is a d-use in that statement. The other options misstate which uses are included.

questions.q: How is program slicing said to help reduce testing effort after modifications?
o: By reducing the cost of regression testing since only the tests that are needed are run
By eliminating the need for any test cases
By replacing coverage reports with slices
By generating new source code automatically
questions.e: In testing, slicing reduces the cost of regression testing after modifications because only those tests that are needed are run. It does not generate code, remove the need for tests, or replace coverage reporting.

questions.q: Among program-slicing tools, which one is described as a program slicer for ANSI C?
o: Unravel
Bandera
Spyder
CodeSurfer
questions.e: Unravel is described as a program slicer for ANSI C. CodeSurfer is GUI-based with a Tk scripting language, Spyder is a debugging tool based on program slicing, and Bandera is the open-source version of the Wisconsin slicer.

questions.q: Which slicing tool is characterized as GUI-based with a Tk scripting language?
o: CodeSurfer
Wisconsin
Unravel
Bandera
questions.e: CodeSurfer is described as GUI-based with a Tk scripting language. Unravel is a slicer for ANSI C, Wisconsin is a slicer for C, and Bandera is the open-source version of Wisconsin.

questions.q: Which tool is identified as an open-source version of the Wisconsin slicer?
o: Unravel
Bandera
Spyder
CodeSurfer
questions.e: Bandera is the open-source version of Wisconsin, which is a slicer for C. Spyder is a debugging tool based on slicing, CodeSurfer is GUI-based with Tk scripting, and Unravel is a slicer for ANSI C.

questions.q: Dataflow-based testing is motivated by the observation that most failures involve which of the following?
o: Exhaustion of the input space
Absence of a control-flow graph
Execution of an incorrect definition
Duplicate use of a killed variable
questions.e: Dataflow testing is premised on the fact that most failures involve execution of an incorrect definition, such as an incorrect assignment/input, an incorrect path caused by a faulty predicate, or a missing (null) definition.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT given as a cause of executing an incorrect definition in dataflow testing?
o: The variable is killed before it is ever defined
The definition is missing (a null definition)
An incorrect path is taken because a predicate is faulty
Incorrect assignment or input statement
questions.e: The three stated causes of an incorrect definition are an incorrect assignment/input statement, an incorrect path taken due to a faulty predicate, and a missing (null) definition. Killing a variable before it is defined is not among the listed causes.

questions.q: What is the stated objective of following the sequence of events related to a given data item in dataflow testing?
o: To remove all null definitions
To guarantee statement coverage
To detect incorrect sequences
To minimize the number of test cases
questions.e: Dataflow testing follows the sequences of events related to a given data item with the objective of detecting incorrect sequences.

questions.q: Dataflow testing explores the effect of what?
o: Killing each variable exactly twice
Using the value produced by every and each computation
Executing only the shortest path
Skipping every branch at least once
questions.e: Dataflow testing explores the effect of using the value produced by every and each computation.

questions.q: What is the first step in the dataflow testing procedure?
o: Write the test cases
Define coverage criteria
Develop the CFG and number the lines/blocks
Identify the DU pairs
questions.e: The steps begin with developing the control-flow graph (CFG) and numbering the lines/blocks, then listing variables, identifying DU pairs, defining coverage criteria, and finally writing test cases.

questions.q: When variables are listed in a table during dataflow testing, which three kinds of marks are recorded?
o: Define (D), Use (CU and PU), and Kill (K)
Read, Write, and Execute
Definition, Predicate, and Branch
Input, Output, and Loop
questions.e: Variables are listed in a table and marked as Define (D), Use split into computation-use (CU) and predicate-use (PU), and Kill (K).

questions.q: In the dataflow testing steps, what immediately follows identifying the DU pairs?
o: Listing the variables in a table
Installing EclEmma
Developing the CFG
Defining coverage criteria considering the test requirement
questions.e: After identifying DU pairs, the next step is to define coverage criteria considering the test requirement, and only then are the test cases written.

questions.q: In the binary-search example, the DCU paths were identified as which of the following node sequences?
questions.e: For the worked binary-search example, the DCU (definition-computation-use) paths were given as 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, while the DU paths were 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7.

questions.q: In the binary-search example, which node sequence was identified as a DU path?
questions.e: The DU paths for the example were given as 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, distinct from the DCU paths of 1, 2, 3, 8, 9.

questions.q: For the test case exercising the variable Top along path 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 (DU path 1 -> 6), which test input was used?
questions.e: The test case for the variable Top used path 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 with DU path 1 -> 6 and the input 3, {1,2,3}, 2 (key 3 searched in array {1,2,3}, returning index 2).

questions.q: For the test case exercising the variable Bottom along path 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 (DU path 1 -> 5), which test input was used?
questions.e: The test case for the variable Bottom used path 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 with DU path 1 -> 5 and the input 1, {1,2,3}, 0 (key 1 searched in array {1,2,3}, returning index 0).

questions.q: In the JUnit test method shown for the binary-search class, the array {1, 2, 3, 4} is searched for key 1 and the assertion expects which result?
questions.e: The test calls mbs.search(key, array) with key = 1 on array {1, 2, 3, 4} and uses assertEquals(0, ...), expecting the returned index to be 0.

questions.q: In the MyBSearch system under test, how are the variables bottom, index, and found initialized?
o: bottom = -1, index = 0, found = true
bottom = 0, index = 0, found = false
bottom = 0, index = -1, found = false
bottom = elemArray.length - 1, index = 0, found = true
questions.e: The search method initializes bottom = 0, top = elemArray.length - 1, index = -1, and found = false before entering the while loop.

questions.q: The loop in the MyBSearch code continues while which condition holds?
o: bottom <= top && found == false
bottom < top || found == true
bottom >= top && found == true
mid <= top && key == found
questions.e: The while loop condition is (bottom <= top && found == false); it terminates when bottom exceeds top or the key is found.

questions.q: Which relationship between coverage criteria is stated as a finding?
o: Statement coverage and branch coverage are equivalent
Branch coverage is weaker than statement coverage
Path coverage is weaker than statement coverage
Statement coverage is weaker than branch coverage
questions.e: A stated finding is that statement coverage is a weaker criterion than branch coverage.

questions.q: According to the findings, what can be determined from coverage analysis?
o: Whether any branches are missed
Which definitions are null
The total execution time of the SUT
The exact number of DU pairs
questions.e: A stated finding is that coverage analysis lets us find out if branches are missed, and that several different coverage reports can be obtained.

questions.q: Which tool is installed in Eclipse to obtain code coverage in this material?
o: Cobertura
EclEmma
JUnit Coverage
JaCoCo standalone
questions.e: EclEmma is the coverage plug-in that is installed in Eclipse to display covered and uncovered code.

questions.q: The summary lists which additional measures as needed to judge whether the generated test cases were enough?
o: Coverage analysis, confidence measure, input space partitioning, and decision tables
Only branch coverage
Random testing and mutation scores
Only statement coverage and path coverage
questions.e: The summary states that beyond deriving and executing test cases, coverage analysis, a confidence measure, input space partitioning, and decision tables were needed to judge test sufficiency.

questions.q: In the dataflow annotation for the worked example, node 4 (the branch if (elemArray[mid] < key)) is marked with which use type?
o: Def = {0}, C-Use = {0}, P-Use = {1}
Def = {1}, C-Use = {1}
Def = {5}, C-Use = {0}, P-Use = {0}
Def = {1}, C-Use = {2}, P-Use = {3}
questions.e: Node 4, corresponding to the predicate if (elemArray[mid] < key), is annotated Def = {0}, C-Use = {0}, P-Use = {1}, reflecting a predicate use with no definition or computation use at that node.

questions.q: Equivalence class testing uses the mathematical concept of equivalence class primarily to generate test cases for which category of testing?
o: Mutation testing
Stress testing
Structural (white-box) testing
Functional (black-box) testing
questions.e: Equivalence class testing applies the mathematical notion of an equivalence class to generate test cases for largely functional (black-box) testing, focusing on program logic rather than the program code.

questions.q: What are the two stated key goals of equivalence class testing?
o: Completeness of test coverage and lessening duplication/effort of coverage
Detecting memory leaks and race conditions
Maximizing code coverage and minimizing runtime
Increasing the number of test cases and their execution speed
questions.e: The two key goals are completeness of test coverage and lessening the duplication (or effort) of test coverage, which mirror the completeness and no-duplication properties of a set partition.

questions.q: For a partitioning of a set A into subsets a1, a2, ..., an, which two conditions must hold?
o: The union of all subsets is empty and the intersection equals A
The subsets must be ordered and overlapping
Each subset must contain exactly one element and all subsets are equal
The union of all subsets equals A (completeness) and every pairwise intersection is empty (no duplication)
questions.e: A valid partition requires a1 U a2 U ... U an = A (completeness) and, for any i and j, ai intersect aj = empty set (no duplication).

questions.q: Which three properties define an equivalence relation on a set A?
o: Commutative, associative, and distributive
Injective, surjective, and bijective
Reflexive, transitive, and antisymmetric
Reflexive, transitive, and symmetric
questions.e: An equivalence relation is defined on set A such that it is reflexive, transitive, and symmetric; equivalence class testing partitions a variable's value set using such a relation.

questions.q: For a numerical input variable whose values range from -200 through +200, using the "= sign" relation the value set is partitioned into which classes?
o: -200 to 0 and 1 to 200 only
Only two classes: valid and invalid
-200 to -1 (negative), 0 (no sign), and 1 to 200 (positive)
questions.e: Using "= sign" as the equivalence relation partitions the -200 to +200 range into -200 to -1 (negative sign), 0 (no sign), and 1 to 200 (positive sign); a sample equivalence test set is (-5, 0, 8).

questions.q: When testing an input range, the three elementary cases to consider are values that are:
o: Within the range, at the boundaries of the range, and outside the range (illegal)
Positive, negative, and zero
Valid, dependent, and impossible
Reflexive, symmetric, and transitive
questions.e: The elementary cases for testing ranges are: within the range, at the boundaries of the range, and outside the range (the illegal region).

questions.q: Weak normal equivalence testing is built on which key assumption about input variables?
o: That there is only a single input variable
That all inputs are invalid
The independence of the input variables
The dependence of the input variables
questions.e: Weak normal equivalence testing assumes the independence of input variables; each variable is partitioned separately and a test case is chosen from each class independently of the other variables.

questions.q: How does strong normal equivalence testing differ from weak normal equivalence testing?
o: It only tests boundary values rather than interior values
It assumes dependence among inputs and includes all combinations of the variables' equivalence classes
It uses fewer test cases by ignoring some classes
It considers invalid inputs while weak normal does not
questions.e: Strong normal equivalence testing is the same as weak normal except that it accounts for dependence among the inputs, so all combinations of the variables' equivalence classes must be included.

questions.q: What distinguishes weak robust equivalence testing from weak normal equivalence testing?
o: Weak robust ignores boundary values entirely
Weak robust requires all combinations of valid inputs
Weak robust assumes dependence among inputs
Weak robust additionally considers the invalid input variables
questions.e: Weak robust is similar to weak normal except that invalid input variables are now considered; a noted difficulty is that invalid inputs may have no specified definition for their output.

questions.q: Strong robust equivalence testing is characterized by which combination of properties?
o: It tests only the boundaries of the valid range
It assumes dependency of input variables and includes invalid inputs, like strong normal but with invalid inputs added
It is identical to weak normal testing
It assumes independence of inputs and only uses valid inputs
questions.e: Strong robust assumes dependency of input variables and is similar to strong normal equivalence testing except that the invalid input variables are now also considered.

questions.q: In the triangle problem, a program accepts 3 integer sides and outputs one of which set of results?
o: Not a triangle, Isosceles, Equilateral, or Scalene
Acute, Obtuse, or Right
Valid or Invalid only
Convex, Concave, or Degenerate
questions.e: The triangle problem accepts 3 input integers for the sides and outputs one of: Not a triangle, Isosceles triangle, Equilateral triangle, or Scalene triangle.

questions.q: In the weak normal triangle example with valid inputs 1 <= a, b, c <= 200, which set of inequalities must hold for the sides to form a triangle?
o: a = b = c
a < b + c, b < a + c, and c < b + a
a > b + c, b > a + c, and c > b + a
questions.e: For the three sides to form a triangle each side must be less than the sum of the other two: a < b + c, b < a + c, and c < b + a.

questions.q: For the triangle problem, why does strong normal equivalence testing yield the same test cases as weak normal equivalence testing?
o: The output has only one possible value
The inputs are strongly dependent on each other
All the inputs are invalid
There are no further sub-intervals inside the valid inputs for the three sides
questions.e: Because there are no further sub-intervals inside the valid input ranges for a, b, and c, strong normal equivalence testing is the same as weak normal equivalence testing for the triangle problem.

questions.q: In the weak robust triangle example, how many invalid test cases are added to the weak normal set?
o: 6 invalid test cases (3 above the range and 3 below)
8 invalid test cases
23 invalid test cases
3 invalid test cases
questions.e: Weak robust adds 6 invalid test cases to the weak normal set: three with a value above the range (e.g., <201,45,50>) and three with a value below the range (e.g., <-5,76,89>).

questions.q: In strong robust equivalence testing for the triangle problem, considering one corner of the input "cube" produces how many invalid cases?
o: 6 cases
3 cases
8 cases, computed as 2^3
7 cases, computed as 2^3 - 1
questions.e: Considering one corner gives (2^3 - 1) = 7 cases of invalids, with another 7 invalids arising from the other diagonal corner <0,0,0>.

questions.q: A decision table is read by columns of rules. If rule R1 has all of its conditions set to True, and it triggers actions a1, a2, and a5, this illustrates that:
o: Each rule column specifies the actions taken for a particular combination of condition values
Rules are read across rows rather than columns
Actions determine the condition values
Only one action can be triggered per rule
questions.e: A decision table is read by columns of rules; R1 says that when all its conditions are True, actions a1, a2, and a5 occur, showing each rule maps a combination of condition values to a set of actions.

questions.q: Why is a decision table said to provide a "completeness check"?
o: It requires no domain knowledge
It always uses only binary conditions
It allows iteration of all the combinations of values of the conditions
It eliminates all impossible cases automatically
questions.e: The decision table allows the iteration of all combinations of the condition values, which provides a completeness check over the possible inputs.

questions.q: In a decision table, the conditions and actions are commonly interpreted as which parts of the system?
o: Conditions as rules and actions as variables
Conditions as inputs and actions as outputs
Both conditions and actions as outputs
Conditions as outputs and actions as inputs
questions.e: The conditions in a decision table may be interpreted as the inputs, and the actions may be thought of as the outputs.

questions.q: For the triangle problem, how is the total of 8 test conditions derived?
o: 3 invalid plus 3 valid conditions
8 valid conditions with no invalid ones
2^3 conditions with no reductions
3 conditions for the not-a-triangle situation plus 5 valid conditions (8 combinations minus 3 impossible)
questions.e: The invalid (not a triangle) situation contributes 3 test conditions, and the valid situation gives 2^3 = 8 minus 3 impossible = 5 conditions; together (3 + 5) = 8 test conditions.

questions.q: A stated disadvantage of decision tables regarding scaling is that for n conditions the number of rules grows as:
o: 2^n rules, becoming worse if the conditions are more than binary
n rules, one per condition
n^2 rules regardless of condition type
Always exactly 8 rules
questions.e: Scaling up can be massive because there are 2^n rules for n conditions if the conditions are binary, and it gets worse when the values are more than binary.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as an advantage of decision table based testing?
o: It guarantees the fewest possible test cases
It requires no domain knowledge to build
It scales effortlessly to any number of conditions
It allows detection of potential errors in the specifications
questions.e: Advantages of decision tables include starting from a complete view, considering dependence/impossible/not-relevant situations to eliminate cases, and detecting potential errors in the specifications; needing domain knowledge and 2^n scaling are disadvantages.

questions.q: What is the concluding view on the relationship between decision table based testing and equivalence class partitioning?
o: Decision tables make equivalence class partitioning unnecessary
Equivalence class partitioning replaces decision tables entirely
They are interchangeable alternatives that produce identical results
They complement each other and should not be treated as alternatives to one another
questions.e: The techniques complement each other and may not be treated as alternatives; decision tables cover positive-intent main-course cases while equivalence class partitioning covers boundary conditions and negative intent.

questions.q: Given the test case format {(inputs), expected output} with 1 < a, b, c < 100, the test case {(101, 0, 0), "Not a triangle"} drew what tester feedback?
o: The output is illogical; the system should instead report that the input is out of bound
The output is correct and needs no change
The inputs are valid and within range
It should be reclassified as an equilateral triangle
questions.e: For {(101, 0, 0), "Not a triangle"}, testers' feedback was that the output is illogical and the system should instead say the input is out of bound, since 101 and 0 fall outside the 1 < value < 100 range.

questions.q: Equivalence class testing develops test cases by partitioning which variable value set into classes using an equivalence relation?
o: The source code statements
Only the output variables' value set
Only the loop counter variables
The input, output, and predicate variables' value set
questions.e: Equivalence class testing develops test cases via the partitioning of the input/output/predicate variables' value set into classes (subsets) using some equivalence relation.

questions.q: In object-oriented software, what is normally considered the 'unit' for unit testing?
o: A cluster of collaborating classes
A single line of code
A class and its methods
A single program, function, or procedure
questions.e: For procedural software the unit is a single program, function, or procedure, but for OO software the unit is a class (and its methods). Unit testing of OO software is therefore intra-class testing, whereas a cluster of classes belongs to integration (inter-class) testing.

questions.q: Why are the individual methods of a class usually tested in the context of their class rather than in isolation?
o: Isolated methods cannot be compiled
Class-level testing is required by UML
Testing single methods separately is usually too expensive due to complex scaffolding
Methods have no state of their own
questions.e: Dealing with single methods separately is usually too expensive because it requires complex scaffolding, so methods are tested in the context of the class they belong to.

questions.q: When a class is represented as a finite state machine, what do the states and transitions correspond to?
o: States correspond to certain values of the attributes; transitions correspond to methods
States correspond to classes; transitions correspond to objects
States correspond to test cases; transitions correspond to inputs
States correspond to methods; transitions correspond to attributes
questions.e: In the finite-state-machine view of a class, states correspond to certain values of the object's attributes, and transitions correspond to the methods that change those values.

questions.q: In FSM-based testing of a class, what form does a test case take?
o: A control-flow graph path
A sequence of method calls that traverse the state machine
A list of attribute values only
A single method call with expected output
questions.e: Test cases are sequences of method calls that traverse the state machine; the idea is to 'drive' the class through all transitions and verify both the response and the resulting state.

questions.q: From which source(s) can a state machine model of a class be derived?
o: Only from the specification
Only from the code
From the specification, from the code (also via reverse engineering), or both
Only from UML sequence diagrams
