A development representative, a testing team representative, and project management
questions.e: The consolidated test report may be output from the bug reporting database, and a meeting is held in which a development representative, a testing team representative, and project management discuss each row of the test execution (test status) report.

questions.q: In JMeter, what are all the test requests (such as HTTP requests and JDBC requests) that are added called?
o: Oracles
Listeners
Samplers
Thread groups
questions.e: In JMeter, all the test requests added, including HTTP requests, user adds, and JDBC requests, are called samplers and are handled as actions.

questions.q: In JMeter, what does adding a 'thread group' represent?
o: The expected output data of a test
A screenshot of a bug
A set of HTTP response listeners
Users, user groups, and their addition strategy
questions.e: A JMeter thread group is where users, user groups, and their addition strategy are configured, along with the number of users and the ramp-up and loop count settings.

questions.q: In the context of scenario-based testing, what is a scenario?
o: A set of automated unit tests bundled together
A hypothetical story used to help a person think through a complex problem or system
A formal mathematical model of the system's state transitions
A prioritized list of code branches to cover
questions.e: A scenario is defined as a hypothetical story used to help a person think through a complex problem or system. It is a narrative device, not a formal model or a coverage list.

questions.q: In which decade did 'scenarios' gain popularity in United States military planning?
o: The 1970's
The 1950's
The 1990's
The 1930's
questions.e: Scenarios gained popularity in United States military planning in the 1950's. Scenario-based planning later gained wide commercial popularity in the early 1970's after success at Royal Dutch/Shell.

questions.q: Scenario-based planning gained wide commercial popularity after a spectacular success at which organization in the early 1970's?
o: A national telecommunications firm
Royal Dutch/Shell
A major automobile manufacturer
The United States military
questions.e: Scenario-based planning gained wide commercial popularity after a spectacular success at Royal Dutch/Shell in the early 1970's. Its former head of scenario planning, Kees van der Heijden, authored 'The Art of Strategic Conversation'.

questions.q: Who is considered a 'stakeholder with influence' in scenario-based testing?
o: A person who can influence development decisions
Anyone at all who is affected by a program
Only the paying customer of the system
Only the developers who write the code
questions.e: Anyone affected by a program is a stakeholder, but a stakeholder with influence is specifically a person who can influence development decisions. Such a stakeholder would push to fix a program that failed a scenario test.

questions.q: What does it mean for a scenario-based test's story to be 'credible'?
o: It could happen in the real world and stakeholders believe something like it probably will happen
It has already occurred at least once during development
It has been formally proven with mathematical logic
It is guaranteed to reveal a coding defect
questions.e: A credible story not only could happen in the real world; stakeholders would believe that something like it probably will happen. Credibility concerns plausibility to stakeholders, not proof or prior occurrence.

questions.q: Why is it especially important that the test results of a scenario be easy to evaluate?
o: Because scenarios are used mainly for unit testing
Because scenarios are complex
Because scenarios are automated and run overnight
Because scenarios only test a single input at a time
questions.e: Easy-to-evaluate results are valuable for all tests but especially important for scenarios because they are complex. A scenario involves a complex use of the program, environment, or set of data.

questions.q: How many types of scenario testing are distinguished, and what is the distinction between them?
o: Four types matching the four levels of testing
Two types: one defines input/output sequences, the other is a script for a sequence of real actions
Two types: one for regression and one for new code
Three types: unit, integration, and system scenarios
questions.e: There are two types of scenario testing. Type 1 uses scenarios to define input/output sequences (close to requirements elicitation), while Type 2 uses scenarios as a script for a sequence of real actions in a real or simulated environment.

questions.q: Which type of scenario testing has quite a lot in common with requirements elicitation?
o: Type 1, which defines input/output sequences
Type 2, which scripts real actions in a real environment
Neither type, because scenario testing avoids requirements
Both types equally, since neither relates to requirements
questions.e: Type 1 scenario testing, which uses scenarios to define input/output sequences, has quite a lot in common with requirements elicitation. Type 2 uses scenarios as a script for a sequence of real actions in a real or simulated environment.

questions.q: The requirements-specification artifact most closely related to writing a good scenario is best described as which of the following?
o: A UML class diagram
A defect density report
A use-case description
A code coverage matrix
questions.e: Much of what is needed to write a good scenario is closely related to what is needed to write a good requirements specification, described as a use-case description. Scenario testing in some sense repeats the requirements process with other people involved.

questions.q: When writing a scenario, what should be done for each identified user after listing possible users?
o: Immediately generate code coverage data for that user
Identify the user's interests and objectives, since a user values a system if it furthers his interests
Assign each user a numeric risk score
Remove the user if they are not a paying customer
questions.e: For each identified user, one identifies his interests and objectives, because a user will value the system if it furthers his interests. The tester then asks how to test that each objective is easy to achieve.

questions.q: In listing system events for a scenario, how is an 'event' defined?
o: Any scheduled maintenance window
Any line of code that changes a variable
Any occurrence that the system is supposed to respond to
Any meeting held with stakeholders
questions.e: An event is any occurrence that the system is supposed to respond to. For a real-time system, anything that generates an interrupt is an event; for each event the tester understands its purpose, what the system should do, and related rules.

questions.q: What characterizes 'special events' that a scenario should account for?
o: They are purely cosmetic and require no handling
They are predictable but unusual and require special handling and circumstances to be triggered
They are undocumented and impossible to predict
They occur constantly and are handled by default logic
questions.e: Special events are predictable but unusual events that require special handling and special circumstances to be triggered. The scenario should include at least the most important of these circumstances.

questions.q: When listing benefits for a scenario, testers are told to watch out for which two problems among stakeholders?
o: Latency and throughput
Memory leaks and race conditions
Misunderstandings and conflicts
Syntax errors and typos
questions.e: When listing benefits, one asks stakeholders for their opinions and watches out for misunderstandings and conflicts, for example between groups of users or between users and customers.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'system requirements' and 'system expectations' when reading about this type of system before writing a scenario?
o: System requirements are what the new system is supposed to do, while system expectations are what other similar systems do
There is no difference; the two terms are interchangeable
System requirements are optional while system expectations are mandatory
System requirements come from books while system expectations come from the customer
questions.e: System requirements describe what the new system is supposed to do, while system expectations describe what other, similar systems do. Knowledge of expectations can be obtained through books, manuals, and similar sources.

questions.q: What is emphasized about creating a mock business for scenario testing?
o: It must be a legally registered company
It should be kept deliberately unrealistic to save time
It should replace all real user observation
It must be realistic even if it isn't real, may need external consultants, and takes a lot of resources
questions.e: A mock business requires good knowledge of how the business works and must be realistic even if it isn't real. It may require external consultants and takes a lot of resources, but can give valuable results.

questions.q: Why is scenario testing considered not good for testing new code?
o: If a bug is hit early, the rest of the test must most likely be postponed until it is fixed
New code cannot be run in a simulated environment
Scenarios only work on compiled binaries
New code has no scenarios associated with it
questions.e: Scenario testing is not good for new code because hitting a bug early in the scenario usually forces the rest of the test to be postponed until the bug is fixed, after which testing resumes until the next bug. For this reason scenario testing should mainly be used as an acceptance test.

questions.q: As what kind of test should scenario testing mainly be used?
o: A regression test
A unit test
An acceptance test
A test of a new bug fix
questions.e: Because scenario testing stalls when an early bug is hit, it should mainly be used as an acceptance test. It is stated to be not useful for regression testing or testing a new fix.

questions.q: What does a scenario test aim to cover, and how does it relate to code coverage?
o: It measures both functional and code coverage equally
It aims to maximize branch coverage of the code
It aims to cover all or part of the system's functionality and does not consider code coverage of any kind
It aims to guarantee 100 percent statement coverage
questions.e: A scenario test aims to cover all or part of the functionality in a system and does not consider code coverage of any kind. Scenario tests discover more design errors than coding errors.

questions.q: Scenario tests tend to discover more of which kind of error?
o: Design errors rather than coding errors
Configuration errors rather than functional errors
Coding errors rather than design errors
Syntax errors rather than logic errors
questions.e: Scenario tests discover more design errors than coding errors. Consequently, they are not useful for tasks such as regression testing or testing a new fix.

questions.q: In scenario testing type 1, the result of writing transactions as sequences of input and expected output can be described as what?
o: An extremely detailed textual use case
A fully automated regression suite
A UML sequence diagram
A code coverage report
questions.e: In type 1 scenario testing, scenarios are used to write transactions as sequences of input and expected output, and the result can be an extremely detailed textual use case.

questions.q: Regarding realism, how is scenario testing type 2 characterized?
o: It is the ultimate testing method for realism, testing behavior in real-world situations with real users and, if necessary, real customers
It avoids real users to keep the test controlled
It is the least realistic method because it uses only simulated data
It is identical in realism to type 1 scenario testing
questions.e: When it comes to realism, scenario testing type 2 is the ultimate testing method. Its goal is to test system behavior in real-world situations with real users supplied by the system owner and, if necessary, real customers.

questions.q: In the procedure for a type 2 scenario test, who reads out each step of the scenario?
o: The lead developer
The system owner
The game master
An automated script runner
questions.e: In a type 2 scenario test, a person called the game master reads out each step of the scenario. Users and customers then react to the situations the game master creates, and the resulting events are documented for later assessment.

questions.q: How are the events resulting from each scenario documented in a type 2 scenario test?
o: By automatically generated log files only
By capturing code coverage metrics during execution
By the users writing their own reports afterward
By a video camera or by one or more observers, for later assessment
questions.e: The events resulting from each scenario are documented, for example by a video camera or by one or more observers, for later assessment. This captures how users and customers reacted to the game master's steps.

questions.q: Since the number of possible scenarios is large and scenario tests are expensive, what determines which scenarios are selected?
o: A random sampling of all scenarios
The alphabetical order of the scenarios
The customer's priorities
The number of lines of code each touches
questions.e: The number of possible scenarios is large, so which scenarios are selected depends on the customer's priorities. Because scenario tests are expensive, usually only a few can be afforded.

questions.q: Scenarios are described as most efficient for testing which kind of requirements?
o: Requirements concerning source code formatting
Requirements about internal algorithm complexity
Requirements about database schema normalization
Requirements involving strong interaction with the system's environment, such as users, customers, networks, file servers, or a stressful work situation
questions.e: Scenarios are most efficient when testing requirements that involve a strong interaction with the system's environment, such as users, customers, networks, file servers, or a stressful work situation.

questions.q: In the order-handling scenario example, what requirement is being tested and what amount of information is on the system's hard disk?
o: Availability of 99.9 percent, with 5 Mb on the hard disk
Response time under 1 second, with 50 Gb on the hard disk
Mean time between failures over 1 year, with 500 Mb on the hard disk
Mean time to repair (MTTR) under 1 hour, with 50 Mb of information on the hard disk
questions.e: The order-handling scenario tests the requirement MTTR (mean time to repair) under 1 hour. The scenario has 50 Mb of information on the system's hard disk when electrical power is suddenly lost during registration of a new order.

questions.q: In the order-handling power-loss scenario, what quantity is measured when the scenario is run one or more times?
o: The time from the power loss until the system is fully operational again
The total disk space consumed after recovery
The number of orders lost per hour
The number of customer phone calls received
questions.e: When the power-loss scenario is run one or more times, the measured quantity is the time from the power loss to when the system is fully operational again. This ties directly to the MTTR-under-1-hour requirement.

questions.q: The order-handling power-loss scenario may identify problems in which of the following areas?
o: Compiler optimization settings
Operational routines such as back-up, operator training for stress handling, and customer handling
Network cabling standards
User interface color schemes
questions.e: The power-loss scenario may identify problems pertaining to operational routines such as back-up, operator training for stress handling, and customer handling, and it raises the question of what happens to the half-filled-in order.

questions.q: From which perspectives can scenarios be viewed?
o: Unit, integration, and regression perspectives
Compilation, linking, and deployment perspectives
System's usage, usability, and functionality validation perspectives
Financial, legal, and marketing perspectives
questions.e: Scenarios can be viewed differently from the system's usage perspective, the usability perspective, and the functionality validation perspective. It is important to determine which of these you are planning to conduct.

questions.q: During which phase of the software lifecycle does regression testing usually refer to testing activities?
o: The requirements gathering phase
The software maintenance phase
The initial design phase
The feasibility study phase
questions.e: Regression testing consists of testing activities that occur after software changes, and it usually refers to testing activities during the software maintenance phase.

questions.q: What are the two major testing objectives of regression testing?
o: Estimate user load and analyze production environment
Encrypt data and prevent information leakage
Design new components and remove obsolete ones
Retest changed components and check the affected parts
questions.e: The major objectives of regression testing are to retest the changed components (or parts) and to check the affected parts (or components) of the system.

questions.q: Software evolving over time may require regression testing for several reasons. Which of the following is one of those stated reasons?
o: Improving documentation formatting
Bug fixing
Reduction of the development team size
Changing the programming language for readability
questions.e: Software evolves over time for reasons including requirements/design changes (new or modified functionality), design changes, bug fixing, and maintenance; regression testing validates that these changes have not caused regression in the rest of the system.

questions.q: If A is the total system and B is a subsystem such that B is a subset of A, which condition is required by the intent of regression testing?
o: B should always be tested independently of any test cases in A
Selecting a subset of test cases for B should exceed the effort to retest A
Retesting of B should equal testing the whole system A
There should not be a case where B caused regression in A and the related test case was skipped
questions.e: The intent requires that retesting B not equal testing all of A, that selecting a subset of B's test cases not exceed the effort to retest A, and that there be no single case where B caused regression in A while its related test case was skipped.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the levels at which regression testing is performed?
o: Re-integration
Regression testing at the encryption level
Regression testing at the database level
Regression testing at the algorithm level
questions.e: Regression testing is performed at different levels: at the unit level, re-integration, at the function level, and at the system level.

questions.q: In the formal definition used for regression testing, if P is a procedure or program and P' is its modified version, what does T represent?
o: A test suite for P
The modification impact set of P'
A new subsystem added to P
A test execution profile for P' only
questions.e: The definition lets P be a procedure or program, P' be a modified version of P, and T be a test suite for P.

questions.q: In the typical regression testing procedure, the first step selects T' (a subset of T, where T' is less than or equal to T) to run on P'. Which regression problem does this step address?
o: The coverage identification problem
The test suite execution problem
The test suite maintenance problem
The regression test selection problem
questions.e: Step 1, selecting T' from T to execute on P', is the regression test selection problem; step 3 addresses coverage identification, steps 2 and 4 address test suite execution, and step 5 addresses test suite maintenance.

questions.q: In the regression testing procedure, which problem is described as updating and storing test information?
o: The coverage identification problem
The test suite execution problem
The regression test selection problem
The test suite maintenance problem
questions.e: Step 5, which creates the new test suite T''' from T, T', and T'', addresses the test suite maintenance problem: the problem of updating and storing test information.

questions.q: Who is stated to perform regression testing at the system level?
o: End users
Test engineers only
Developers only
QA and test engineers
questions.e: Developers perform regression testing at the unit level or integration, test engineers perform it at the function level, and QA and test engineers perform it at the system level.

questions.q: Which artifact is identified as needed to perform software regression testing?
o: The marketing plan for the product
The original project cost estimate
Software change information (change notes)
The developer's personal notes only
questions.e: The artifacts needed include software change information (change notes), updated requirements/design specifications and user manuals, the regression testing process and strategy, and the regression testing methods and criteria.

questions.q: When selecting a subset of test cases from an existing test suite for regression, into which three categories are the test cases classified?
o: Re-testable, reusable, and obsolete
Passing, failing, and blocked
Functional, structural, and random
Unit, integration, and system
questions.e: Selecting a subset of test cases from the existing suite involves classifying them as re-testable, reusable, or obsolete, along with adding new test cases.

questions.q: In the illustrative example of a method int ageCalc(date dateOfBirth) that needs updating, from how many different methods of the class is this function called, demonstrating that one change can impact the whole class?
questions.e: The example states the ageCalc method is called from all 21 different methods of the class, so a change in one method creates an impact across the whole class.

questions.q: What principle is stated about the cost of test case selection for regression testing?
o: It should equal the cost of writing new test cases
It should always exceed the cost of running the whole suite
It is unrelated to the cost of running the whole suite
It should not be more than re-running the whole test suite
questions.e: A major challenge is to minimize re-testing effort while achieving adequate coverage; the test case selection cost for regression testing should not be more than re-running the whole test suite.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as an effect of maintenance in regression testing?
o: Delete existing function features
Change algorithm logic
Add new functional features
Change component interactions
questions.e: Effects of maintenance include changing state-based behaviors, component interfaces, database design, GUI design, function design, low-level design documents, algorithm logic, and component structure. Adding new features and deleting features are instead listed under effects of requirement change.

questions.q: In the bug-fixing example, why does Developer Y experience a regression without knowing it?
o: Developer X added a column to a shared database table and the manager forgot to disseminate the change
Developer Y deleted a shared class by mistake
The database server crashed during testing
Developer Y's compiler was out of date
questions.e: Developer X added a column to a table in a shared backend database; the manager approved it but forgot to inform the team, so Developer Y's code, which accessed that table, regressed without his knowledge.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the regression testing process flow that begins with software change?
o: Build Test Suite, Software Change Analysis, Run Tests, Report Results
Define Strategy, Software Change Analysis, Report Results, Run Tests, Build Suite
Software Change Analysis, Software Change Impact Analysis, Define Regression Testing Strategy, Build Regression Test Suite, Run Regression Tests, Report Retest Results
Run Regression Tests, Software Change Impact Analysis, Build Test Suite, Report Results
questions.e: The flow proceeds from Software Change Analysis to Software Change Impact Analysis, then Define Regression Testing Strategy, Build Regression Test Suite, Run Regression Tests at different levels, and finally Report Retest Results.

questions.q: Methods of regression testing work on the basis of change identification and test selection. Through which two techniques is test selection achieved?
o: Load testing and stress testing
Test case recording and test case deletion
Coverage analysis and crowd testing
Test case minimization and test case prioritization
questions.e: Methods of regression testing rely on change identification and on test selection through test case minimization and test case prioritization.

questions.q: Among the methods for regression test selection, which two are described as the opposite extremes?
o: Modification based selection and coverage based selection
Re-test all and random retesting
Unit testing and system testing
Test case minimization and test case prioritization
questions.e: The regression test selection methods range from re-test all (one extreme) through modification-based and coverage-based selection to random retesting (the other extreme).

questions.q: Why is regression test case selection described as application specific, using examples such as a nuclear power plant versus an attendance system?
o: Because different applications use different programming languages
Because the range/criticality of the application suggests whether to retest all or use selective retesting
Because only critical applications can afford any testing
Because attendance systems cannot be regression tested
questions.e: Test case selection requires prior knowledge of the application type; the range of application (e.g., nuclear power plant, medical equipment, banking, attendance system) suggests whether regression testing should be retest-all or selective retesting based on a selection method.

questions.q: One cited approach uses an Extended Finite State Machine considering control and data dependence to construct a state dependence graph that identifies the effect of modification. Which work is this attributed to?
o: Khan TA et al, 2012
Korel et al, 2002
Chen et al, 2006
Briand et al, 2009
questions.e: Chen et al (2006) used an Extended Finite State Machine considering control and data dependence to construct a state dependence graph used to identify the effect of modification.

questions.q: Which cited approach analyzes UML designs where pre- and post-conditions are given as OCL constraints and model changes are analyzed via their XML representation?
o: Chen et al, 2006
Briand et al, 2009
Khan TA et al, 2012
Korel et al, 2002
questions.e: Briand et al (2009) considered UML designs with pre- and post-conditions given as OCL constraints, analyzing model changes by analyzing their XML representation.

questions.q: What does test case prioritization aim to do in regression testing?
o: Merge multiple test suites into a single test case
Delete all previously failing test cases
Order previously run test cases according to a requirement, such as maximum node coverage first
Convert manual test cases into automated ones
questions.e: Test case prioritization orders previously run test cases according to a requirement; for example, reordering so the test case providing maximum coverage with respect to nodes is selected first.

questions.q: Given the three test cases 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10; 1,2,3,5,6,7,6,8,9,10; and 1,2,3,5,6,8,10, if they are prioritized by the number of nodes covered, which is selected first?
o: They all cover the same number of nodes
questions.e: When prioritized by the number of nodes covered, the test case 1,2,3,5,6,7,6,8,9,10 is selected first, followed by 1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10, and then 1,2,3,5,6,8,10.

questions.q: One test case prioritization technique sorts test cases in order of increasing cost per additional coverage, selects the first, and repeats. Until when is this repeated?
o: Until no test cases remain in the suite
Until n test cases are selected
Until all edges are covered
Until the total cost reaches zero
questions.e: The technique sorts test cases by increasing cost per additional coverage, selects the first test case, and repeats these two steps until n test cases are selected; cost decisions can be based on individual or cumulative test case cost.

questions.q: Which statement about Selenium, as used for recording web test cases, is correct?
o: It supports only the C# language
It cannot simulate a user navigating through pages
It only works in environments where JavaScript is disabled
It is a set of tools supporting rapid development of test automation for web-based applications and works anywhere JavaScript is supported
questions.e: Selenium is a set of tools that supports rapid development of test automation for web-based applications, works anywhere JavaScript is supported, supports languages such as Java, Ruby, and Python, and can simulate a user navigating pages and assert for specific marks.

questions.q: How is load testing characterized?
o: As a type of non-functional testing that studies SUT behavior under a specific expected load, including normal and peak conditions
As a usability test targeting the intended audience
As a security test ensuring no information leakage
As a type of functional testing that checks each component individually
questions.e: Load testing is a type of non-functional testing conducted to understand the behavior of the system under test under a specific expected load, determining behavior under both normal and peak conditions.

questions.q: Verification is best described as which kind of process?
o: A process that only applies to released software after deployment
A static process that assesses a product or system during a phase against the requirements specified for that phase
A process led exclusively by management to approve budgets
A dynamic process that executes the software to observe its behavior
questions.e: Verification is a static process that assesses a software product or system during a particular phase to determine whether it meets the requirements or conditions specified at the beginning of that phase. It substantiates artifacts such as the SRS, SDS, design, and code without executing the software.

questions.q: Which artifacts are substantiated (checked) during verification?
o: Marketing and sales documentation
SRS, SDS, design, and code/program
Only the final compiled binary
Only user acceptance test results
questions.e: As a static process, verification substantiates artifacts including the SRS, SDS, design, and the code/program, rather than executing the software.

questions.q: If fixing a bug found during the specification phase costs $1 and the cost grows tenfold at each later stage, what is the approximate cost to fix a bug found only in released software?
questions.e: The cost to fix a bug increases exponentially (roughly tenfold) as time passes: $1 in specification, $10 in design, $100 in code, and $1000 when found in released software.

questions.q: Which pairing correctly matches a verification/quality method category with its meaning?
o: Defect prevention = error blocking and error source removal
Defect removal = safety assurance through redundancy
Defect prevention = fault tolerance and failure containment
Defect containment = error blocking and error source removal
questions.e: Defect prevention is error blocking and error source removal; defect removal is inspection and testing; defect containment is fault tolerance and failure containment (safety assurance).

questions.q: Under the categorization of verification approaches, which category does inspection belong to?
o: Defect injection
Defect prevention
Defect containment
Defect removal
questions.e: Defect removal covers inspection and testing. Defect prevention is error blocking and error source removal, while defect containment is fault tolerance and failure containment.

questions.q: The three main verification methods discussed are peer reviews, walkthroughs, and which third method?
o: Inspections
Static code compilation
Unit testing
Regression testing
questions.e: Verification methods are mainly divided into peer reviews, walkthroughs, and inspections. Testing is a defect removal technique but is not listed among these three review-based verification methods.

questions.q: In a walkthrough, who leads the review process?
o: A member of management
The author of the artifact under review
A trained moderator who is not the author
An external auditor with no team ties
questions.e: In a walkthrough, the author of the artifact leads the review process, while team members ask questions and spot possible errors. The meeting is usually led by the author of the document under review.

questions.q: What is stated as the main purpose of a walkthrough?
o: To enable learning about the document's content, help members understand it, and also find defects
To assign blame for defects to specific authors
To measure exact defect removal percentages
To formally certify the artifact for release
questions.e: The main purpose of a walkthrough is to enable learning about the content of the document under review, helping team members understand it and also find defects. Its result quality depends on the personal brilliance of the reviewer.

questions.q: In a walkthrough, the quality of the results is said to depend primarily on what?
o: The number of checklists applied
The size of the moderator's report
The formal entry and exit criteria
The personal brilliance of the reviewer
questions.e: For walkthroughs, the quality of results depends upon the personal brilliance of the reviewer, since the process is comparatively informal and author-led.

questions.q: Which statement about a peer review is correct?
o: It is always led by the author of the artifact
It is led by a trained moderator who is NOT the author
It excludes technical specialists from the process
It requires management participation to be valid
questions.e: A peer review is usually led by a trained moderator who is not the author, does not involve management participation, and includes peers and technical specialists in the review process.

questions.q: How many professionals are involved in a peer review team?
o: About 4 persons only
A team of 3 to 6 members
A team of 8 to 10 professionals
A team of 2 to 7 professionals
questions.e: A peer review involves a team of 2 to 7 professionals, requires authors to present their work, and produces a report (optional to the author) presenting issues as a few faults.

questions.q: In the issue classification used for reviews, how is a 'Moderate' defect defined?
o: A defect that can be overlooked with no loss of functionality
A defect that always blocks release
A defect affecting limited areas of functionality that can be worked around or ignored
A defect that may cause incorrect results or behavior
questions.e: Moderate defects affect limited areas of functionality that can either be worked around or ignored. Severe defects may cause incorrect results or behavior, and minor defects can be overlooked with no loss of functionality.

questions.q: Who defined inspections, and in what year?
o: M. E. Fagan of IBM in 1976
B. Boehm of TRW in 1981
W. E. Deming of Bell Labs in 1986
S. H. Kan of IBM in 1976
questions.e: M. E. Fagan of IBM defined inspections in 1976. Inspection is the most formal review method, led by a trained moderator who is not the author, and driven by checklists and rules.

questions.q: Which characteristic distinguishes an inspection as the most formal review method?
o: It permits results to depend on the reviewer's personal brilliance
It is driven by checklists and rules and uses entry and exit criteria
It requires management to act as moderator
It is led by the author and uses no checklists
questions.e: Inspection is the most formal review method: it is led by a trained moderator (not the author), driven by checklists and rules, and makes use of entry and exit criteria.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of all defects can inspections find?
o: About 10%
About 60%
About 90%
About 30%
questions.e: Inspections can find about 60% of all defects. They are technical rather than management activities, and their results can assess or improve the quality of the work product, the development process, and the review process.

questions.q: How many members are stated to make up an inspection team?
o: A team of 3 to 6 members
A team of 2 to 7 members
Exactly 10 members
A single moderator working alone
questions.e: An inspection involves a team of 3 to 6 members, requires a formal presenter in the form of a moderator (not the author), prior preparation of the complete team, and a formal report by the moderator.

questions.q: Regarding defect removal cost, upstream defect removal is said to be how much cheaper?
o: 1000 times cheaper
10-100 times cheaper
About the same cost
2-5 times cheaper
questions.e: Upstream defect removal is 10-100 times cheaper. Inspections reduce total project cost despite their own execution costs, and reviews also disseminate domain knowledge, development skills, and corporate culture.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the six steps in a Fagan Inspection?
o: Overview, Planning, Inspection, Preparation, Follow-up, Rework
Planning, Overview, Preparation, Inspection, Rework, Follow-up
Planning, Preparation, Overview, Rework, Inspection, Follow-up
Preparation, Planning, Inspection, Overview, Follow-up, Rework
questions.e: The Fagan Inspection steps in order are: 1. Planning, 2. Overview (1-to-n meeting), 3. Preparation (individual inspection), 4. Inspection (n-to-n meeting), 5. Rework, and 6. Follow-up.

questions.q: In a Fagan Inspection, what is the recommended team size set during the Planning step?
o: About 4 persons
2 to 7 persons
Exactly 6 persons
A single inspector
questions.e: During the Planning step of a Fagan Inspection, the team size is set at about 4 persons, drawn from developers/testers on similar projects, with inspectors who are not the authors.

questions.q: During the Inspection (collection) meeting step of a Fagan Inspection, what is the focus and time limit?
o: Reworking defects, lasting a full working day
Defect identification but not solutions, lasting no more than 2 hours
Assigning individual tasks, lasting 30 minutes
Providing defect solutions, with no time limit
questions.e: The Fagan Inspection meeting collects and consolidates individual results with a reader/presenter paraphrasing the material; it focuses on defect identification but not solutions and should take no more than 2 hours, producing an inspection report.

questions.q: In a Fagan Inspection, what happens during the Rework step, and who verifies resolution during Follow-up?
o: Entry criteria are set; management verifies resolution
Inspectors independently examine code; the customer verifies resolution
The moderator fixes defects; the author verifies resolution
The author responds and fixes defects; the moderator verifies resolution
questions.e: Rework is where the author responds and fixes the defects (provides solutions). Follow-up then handles resolution verification by the moderator and a decision about possible re-inspection.

questions.q: Why are checklists considered valuable in verification and inspections?
o: They guarantee zero defects will remain after inspection
They represent time-tested means of ensuring nothing is forgotten and capture industrial best practices and lessons learnt
They are language-independent and apply identically to every artifact
They replace the need for any human reviewers
questions.e: Checklists represent a time-tested means of making sure nothing is forgotten in a process, capturing industrial best practices as templates and providing access to a preexisting knowledge base and lessons learnt.

questions.q: According to the material, code inspection checklists have what important characteristic?
o: They are identical across all programming languages
They only apply to the SRS
They are language specific
They are optional and rarely used
questions.e: Code checklists are language specific. An example code inspection checklist covers areas such as code formatting (alignment, block start/end identifiability, naming conventions), structure, variables, comments, loops and branches, and general items.

questions.q: Which of the following is an item on the Functional Requirements Checklist for SRS inspections?
o: Are proper left-margin alignments followed?
Are all inputs to a function sufficient to perform the required function?
Are all screen shots accurate and complete?
Is there an else block for every if clause?
questions.e: The Functional Requirements Checklist for SRS inspections asks whether all inputs to a function are sufficient to perform the required function, alongside items about specified customer requirements, undesired events/inputs, use case descriptions, and misuse cases.

questions.q: Which naming conventions are mentioned as examples in the code formatting portion of a code inspection checklist?
o: Snake_case, kebab-case, and dot.notation
Reverse notation and prefix notation
UPPERCASE, lowercase, and Title Case only
Pascal, CamelCase, and Hungarian notation
questions.e: The code formatting checklist asks whether naming conventions such as Pascal, CamelCase, and Hungarian notation are followed, along with checks for proper left-margin alignment and easily identifiable code block start/end points.

questions.q: Which item appears on the checklist used in the Code Review Example?
o: All screen shots accurately display the current version of the software
All requirements communicated by the customer have been specified
There is an else block for every if clause even if it is empty
All charts and diagrams are labeled consistently
questions.e: The code review checklist includes requiring an else block for every if clause even if empty, plus items like following coding conventions, no commented-out or dead code, checking arrays for out of bounds, and properly closing files/sockets/cursors.

questions.q: In the Code Review Example, which severity level was assigned to 'Try-catch block not implemented'?
o: Minor
Severe
Trivial
Moderate
questions.e: In the Code Review Example's issues found, a missing try-catch block was classified as Severe, a missing constructor and missing comments were Moderate, and not following a naming convention (e.g., Hungarian notation) was Minor.

questions.q: Which resources are listed as needed to conduct the Code Review Example?
o: Only a compiler and test data
Only the author and the customer
Moderator, team members, authors, checklists, reporting forms, and the code artifact
A test harness and automated coverage tools
questions.e: The Code Review Example requires a moderator, team members, authors, checklists, reporting forms, and the artifact (code) for inspection/review, with the author presenting the code while the moderator conducts planning, overview, preparation, and inspection with two team members.

questions.q: What is stated about the relationship between each lifecycle stage and verification?
o: Verification is performed only after all stages complete
Each step in the development lifecycle requires verification before an artifact becomes a milestone and moves to the next stage
Verification replaces the need for a defined lifecycle
Verification is only needed once, before release
questions.e: Each step in the adopted application development lifecycle requires verification before an artifact becomes a milestone and goes to the next stage. Applications of verification include SRS verification, design verification, and code verification.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a software development lifecycle model in the context of software verification?
o: Kanban board model
Spiral model
Fagan model
Six Sigma model
questions.e: Listed lifecycle models include the Waterfall model, Spiral model, Rapid Application Development (RAD), and Evolutionary prototyping. Each stage can contain issues such as misconceptions, misunderstandings, and errors.

questions.q: What is penetration (pen) testing best described as?
o: A technique for optimizing database query performance
The process of documenting functional requirements before coding begins
The process of finding and reporting security vulnerabilities in a network, computer, or software application in order to secure it against attacks
A method of measuring code coverage of unit tests
questions.e: Penetration testing is the process of finding and reporting security vulnerabilities in a network, computer, or software application in order to secure it against any sort of attacks. The other options describe unrelated software activities.

questions.q: In white box penetration testing, what level of access and knowledge does the tester have?
o: Only limited information to attack the system externally
Complete access and in-depth knowledge of the system to be tested
Access only to the physical premises but not the software
No knowledge at all of the system or network
questions.e: In white box penetration testing the tester has complete access and in-depth knowledge of the system, which is very helpful for carrying out extensive penetration testing. Having no knowledge describes black box, and limited information describes gray box.

questions.q: Which penetration testing approach leaves the tester totally unaware of the system or network and, as a result, might miss some areas while testing?
o: Gray box penetration testing
Reconnaissance penetration testing
Black box penetration testing
White box penetration testing
questions.e: In black box penetration testing only high-level information is made available and the tester is totally unaware of the system/network, so this approach might miss some areas while testing. White box has full knowledge and gray box has limited knowledge.

questions.q: Gray box penetration testing is characterized by which of the following?
o: No information whatsoever is provided to the tester
Only limited information is made available to the tester to attack the system externally
The tester has complete access and in-depth knowledge of the system
The tester is given the full source code and network diagrams
questions.e: Gray box penetration testing makes only limited information available to the tester to attack the system externally. Complete access describes white box, while no information describes black box.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of penetration testing phases?
o: Threat Modelling, Scanning/Reconnaissance, Exploitation, Vulnerability Analysis, Post-Exploitation Reporting
Scanning/Reconnaissance, Threat Modelling, Vulnerability Analysis, Exploitation, Post-Exploitation Reporting
Exploitation, Threat Modelling, Scanning/Reconnaissance, Vulnerability Analysis, Post-Exploitation Reporting
Vulnerability Analysis, Scanning/Reconnaissance, Threat Modelling, Post-Exploitation Reporting, Exploitation
questions.e: The penetration testing steps proceed as Scanning/Reconnaissance, then Threat Modelling, then Vulnerability Analysis, then Exploitation, and finally Post-Exploitation Reporting. The other sequences reorder these phases incorrectly.

questions.q: The penetration testing phase focused on getting to know the target using passive methods and gathering as much information as possible is called what?
o: Threat Modelling
Exploitation
Scanning / Reconnaissance
Post-Exploitation Reporting
questions.e: Scanning/Reconnaissance involves getting to know the target using passive methods, with the idea of gathering as much info about the subject as possible (for example, search engine queries). Threat Modelling, Exploitation, and Reporting are later phases.

questions.q: Which penetration testing phase is described as a pre-attack phase in which a model of all the security concerns is produced and everything is made ready?
o: Scanning / Reconnaissance
Exploitation
Vulnerability Analysis
Threat Modelling
questions.e: Threat Modelling produces a description or model of all the security concerns and why they should be resolved; it is a pre-attack phase in which everything is made ready. Vulnerability Analysis and Exploitation come afterward.

questions.q: In the penetration testing phases, what does the Vulnerability Analysis phase involve?
o: Detailing the vulnerabilities found and their potential impact
Gathering info about the target using passive methods
Gaining access by breaching security or finding a bug to exploit
Identifying vulnerabilities and determining their severity
questions.e: Vulnerability Analysis is about identifying vulnerabilities and determining their severity. Gaining access is Exploitation, detailing findings is Post-Exploitation Reporting, and passive info gathering is Reconnaissance.

questions.q: The Exploitation phase of penetration testing is defined as which of the following?
o: Identifying vulnerabilities and determining their severity
Gaining access by breaching the security of a system or finding a bug to exploit in the software
Modelling all the security concerns and why they should be resolved
Detailing the vulnerabilities found and providing information on potential impact
questions.e: Exploitation means gaining access by breaching the security of a system or finding a bug to exploit in the software. Determining severity is Vulnerability Analysis, detailing findings is Post-Exploitation Reporting, and modelling concerns is Threat Modelling.

questions.q: In the classification of pen testers, which type has no prior knowledge of the network, computer, or application to be tested?
o: Black Hat
Red Hat
White Hat
Gray Hat
questions.e: A Black Hat tester works with no prior knowledge of the network, computer, or application. A White Hat has complete knowledge, and a Gray Hat has limited knowledge.

questions.q: Which classification of pen tester works with complete knowledge of the network, computer, or application to be tested?
o: Blue Hat
Black Hat
White Hat
Gray Hat
questions.e: A White Hat tester has complete knowledge of the target, whereas a Black Hat has no prior knowledge and a Gray Hat has limited knowledge.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a Network Vulnerability Assessment tool rather than a Web Vulnerability Assessment tool?
o: Sqlmap
OWASP ZAP
Nmap
Acunetix
questions.e: Nmap is listed among the Network Vulnerability Assessment tools (along with OpenVAS, Wireshark, Metasploit, and MBSA). OWASP ZAP, Acunetix, and Sqlmap are Web Vulnerability Assessment tools.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Web Vulnerability Assessment tool?
o: Burp suite
MBSA
Wireshark
OpenVAS
questions.e: Burp suite is listed among the Web Vulnerability Assessment tools (with OWASP ZAP, Acunetix, Nikto, and Sqlmap). Wireshark, OpenVAS, and MBSA are Network Vulnerability Assessment tools.

questions.q: What does MBSA stand for among the network vulnerability assessment tools?
o: Managed backup security agent
Malware behavior scanning application
Modular breach simulation analyzer
Microsoft baseline security analyzer
questions.e: MBSA stands for Microsoft baseline security analyzer, one of the listed network vulnerability assessment tools alongside Nmap, OpenVAS, Wireshark, and Metasploit.

questions.q: What is a key difference between a pen tester and a hacker regarding approval?
o: Neither pen testers nor hackers require any approval
Pen testers have prior approval from senior management, while hackers have prior approval only from themselves
Both pen testers and hackers require prior approval from senior management
Pen testers approve themselves while hackers require management approval
questions.e: Pen testers have prior approval from senior management, whereas hackers have prior approval only from themselves. Their social engineering also differs: pen testers aim to raise awareness while hackers aim to trick systems into divulging sensitive information.

questions.q: In the contrast between ethical hacking and penetration testing, which pairing is correct?
o: Both ethical hacking and pen testing are purely defensive measures
Ethical hacking defends the system while pen testing breaks into it
Ethical hacking is an offensive measure whose main target is to break into the system, while pen testing is a defensive measure whose main target is to defend the system
Ethical hacking is defensive while pen testing is offensive
questions.e: Ethical hacking is an offensive measure whose main target is to break into the system, while penetration testing is a defensive measure whose main target is to defend the system against any threat. The other options reverse these roles.

questions.q: Penetration testing is said to produce what kind of result?
o: A binary result: either the team owned you, or they didn't
A ranked list of code smells
A statistical confidence interval
A continuous numeric risk score between 0 and 100
questions.e: Penetration testing produces a binary result, meaning either the team owned you or they didn't. It is described as highly accurate and reliable and serves as a proof of concept against vulnerabilities.

questions.q: In the worked penetration testing example, which open-source web application security scanner was used to scan the application?
o: Wireshark packet analyzer
Microsoft Baseline Security Analyzer
Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP), the OWASP scanner
Nmap network mapper
questions.e: The worked example scanned the application against the ZAP OWASP scanner; Zed Attack Proxy is an open-source web application security scanner that produced a list of potential vulnerabilities. Nmap, Wireshark, and MBSA are network tools not used in that example.

questions.q: According to the definition attributed to Cem Kaner, exploratory testing emphasizes which of the following?
o: The personal freedom and responsibility of the individual tester to continually optimize the quality of their work
Full automation of every test with no human intervention
Strict adherence to pre-written test cases determined in advance
Formal proof of program correctness
questions.e: Exploratory testing, per the cited definition, emphasizes the personal freedom and responsibility of the individual tester to continually optimize the quality of their work, treating learning, test design, execution, and interpretation as parallel, mutually supportive activities. Pre-written test cases and formal proofs are not part of it.

questions.q: Which statement correctly characterizes exploratory testing?
o: It is not a technique but an approach, where what you do next is governed by what you are doing currently
It requires test logging to be completed before any execution begins
It is a formal technique requiring all test cases to be written before execution
It forbids documenting defects during test execution
questions.e: Exploratory testing is described as not a technique but an approach, in which the next actions are governed by what you are currently doing. Test logging is performed at the same time as test execution, and defects and further-testing thoughts are documented during that logging.

questions.q: What are the four phases of exploratory testing in order?
o: Test Design, Learn, Analysis, Test Execution
Learn, Test Design, Test Execution, Analysis
Analysis, Learn, Test Design, Test Execution
Learn, Test Execution, Test Design, Analysis
questions.e: The four exploratory testing phases are Learn, then Test Design, then Test Execution, then Analysis. In Test Design a brief test description is produced rather than full test cases, and in Analysis the tester reflects on what was learned about the product and the testing.

questions.q: In the Test Design phase of exploratory testing, what is produced?
o: A brief test description rather than test cases
A binary pass/fail proof of concept
A threat model of security concerns
A complete formal set of test cases with expected results
questions.e: The Test Design phase of exploratory testing yields a brief test description rather than formal test cases. Formal test cases belong to structured testing, and threat modelling belongs to penetration testing.

questions.q: When contrasting structured testing with exploratory testing, which pairing is correct?
o: Neither approach determines any test cases
Structured testing determines test cases well in advance, while exploratory testing determines test cases during testing
Both determine all test cases only after testing is complete
Structured testing determines test cases during testing, while exploratory testing determines them well in advance
questions.e: In structured testing, test cases are determined well in advance, whereas in exploratory testing they are determined during testing. Structured testing also emphasizes prediction, confirmation, and controlling tests, while exploratory testing emphasizes adaptability, investigation, and improving test design.

questions.q: Which characteristic is associated with exploratory testing rather than structured testing?
o: It emphasizes adaptability and learning and is about improvement of test design
It determines all test cases well in advance
It confirms testing strictly against requirements only
It emphasizes prediction and decision making and is about controlling tests
questions.e: Exploratory testing emphasizes adaptability and learning and is about the improvement of test design, involving investigation of the system. Emphasizing prediction/decision making, controlling tests, and determining test cases in advance are traits of structured testing.
